items.title: SNCFT | Perturbations sur le trafic ferroviaire
items.description: La Société nationale des chemins de fer tunisiens (SNCFT) annonce, ce vndredi 7 août 2026, une perturbation du trafic ferroviaire à l'entrée sud de Tunis. Le mouvement des trains est actuellement perturbé dans les deux sens entre les gares de Tunis et de Jbel Jelloud, impactant aussi bien la ligne des banlieues sud que les lignes de grandes distances, indique un communiqué de la SNCFT, ajoutant que la circulation s'effectue momentanément sur une voie unique. Cette situation est causée par deux facteurs simultanés : une panne électrique sur le câble de la deuxième voie et des travaux d'aménagement sur la troisième voie, menés dans le cadre du projet d'élargissement de l'entrée sud de la capitale. Tout en présentant ses excuses à sa clientèle pour la gêne occasionnée, la SNCFT précise que ses équipes techniques sont actuellement mobilisées sur le terrain pour effectuer les réparations nécessaires et rétablir la circulation normale dans les plus meilleurs délais. Y. N. L’article SNCFT | Perturbations sur le trafic ferroviaire est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: West Africa Champions Cup 2026 : neuf clubs ouest-africains attendus pour la 5ème édition
items.description: La 5e édition de la West Africa Champions Cup se déroulera du 14 au 22 août 2026 au stade M’Ballou Mady Diakité de Kankan. L’annonce a été faite ce vendredi 7 août par les organisateurs, à l’occasion d’une conférence de presse consacrée aux préparatifs de la compétition. Initialement annoncée avec la participation de dix clubs, cette édition réunira finalement neuf formations après le forfait de dernière minute du club soudanais d’Al Hilal SC. La Guinée sera représentée par trois clubs : le Horoya AC, le Hafia FC et le Karfamoriah FC. Le Mali, pays le plus représenté, alignera quatre équipes : le Djoliba AC, le Stade Malien, le Real de Bamako et le FC Diarra. La Sierra Leone sera présente avec Star Sport, tandis que la Mauritanie sera représentée par le FC NZidane. Créée il y a cinq ans, la West Africa Champions Cup vise principalement à offrir aux clubs de la sous-région une meilleure préparation avant le lancement des championnats nationaux et des compétitions interclubs de la CAF. Pour le promoteur de la compétition, Alpha Mady Touré, cette vision demeure le fondement du tournoi. « Le tournoi est né du constat selon lequel nos clubs avaient un déficit de préparation avant les compétitions interclubs de la CAF », a-t-il expliqué. Selon lui, l’engouement suscité par la compétition auprès des clubs confirme son utilité. Il cite notamment la participation régulière du Djoliba AC et du Stade Malien, qui ont fait de ce rendez-vous un élément important de leur préparation. « Le Stade Malien s’est préparé depuis trois ans dans cette compétition », a-t-il rappelé, tout en soulignant l’intérêt constant des clubs guinéens pour le tournoi. Cette 5e édition a néanmoins été confrontée à des difficultés financières et logistiques. Les organisateurs indiquent avoir reçu plusieurs demandes de participation, sans pouvoir toutes les satisfaire. « Nous avons eu énormément de sollicitations, mais avec les contraintes financières et logistiques, nous avons été obligés de nous limiter à neuf clubs », a précisé Alpha Mady Touré. Le co-promoteur Cellou Tâta Diallo a, pour sa part, insisté sur les défis liés à l’organisation, notamment la prise en charge des délégations étrangères. « Dieu sait combien il est compliqué de prendre en charge ne serait-ce qu’une seule équipe », a-t-il déclaré. Après plusieurs éditions organisées dans différentes localités, la West Africa Champions Cup revient pour la troisième fois à Kankan. Pour les promoteurs, ce choix traduit la volonté de contribuer à la promotion du football à l’intérieur du pays et de rapprocher les grandes compétitions sportives des populations. Présente à la conférence de presse, la Fédération Guinéenne de Football a salué l’initiative. Son secrétaire général, Ibrahima Blasco Barry, a estimé que ce tournoi constitue un cadre précieux pour renforcer la préparation des clubs et favoriser les échanges sportifs entre les pays de la sous-région. À l’approche du démarrage des compétitions interclubs de la CAF, cette nouvelle édition devrait ainsi permettre aux équipes participantes de peaufiner leurs automatismes, d’évaluer leur niveau et de se mesurer à des adversaires issus de différents championnats ouest-africains.

items.title: KNUST marks 75th anniversary with medical, one health outreach at Anwomaso
items.description: The Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Kumasi (KNUST) has reaffirmed its commitment to community service and public health through a comprehensive Medical and One Health Outreach organised by its College of Health Sciences as part of the University’s 75th Anniversary celebrations. Prof. Francis Kemausuor Dean of the Faculty of Mechanical and Chemical Engineering, speaking on behalf of the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Christian Agyare, said KNUST’s 75th anniversary was not only an opportunity to reflect on its achievements in teaching, research and innovation but also to demonstrate its enduring responsibility to society. “KNUST’s seventy-five-year journey has been defined not only by excellence in teaching, research and innovation, but also by a strong commitment to service,” he said, adding that, as a public university, KNUST has a duty to ensure its knowledge and expertise directly improve the well-being of communities. He described the outreach as “a practical demonstration of that responsibility,” noting that it brought together professionals and students from various health disciplines to deliver integrated healthcare services to surrounding communities. Prof. Kemausuor commended the College of Health Sciences, the planning committee and participating schools and departments for collaborating to organise the outreach, stressing that multidisciplinary collaboration is essential to addressing today’s complex health challenges. He also expressed appreciation to traditional authorities, market leaders, community members and development partners for supporting the initiative through logistical assistance, equipment and supplies. Prof. Kemausuor urged health professionals, students and volunteers to deliver services with professionalism, compassion and respect while protecting patient confidentiality and ensuring that participants requiring further care received appropriate referrals. He encouraged residents to take full advantage of the available services by asking questions, providing accurate health information and following medical advice after the screening exercises. He noted that health screening is most effective when followed by appropriate action and continued care. Professor Fred Stephen Sarfo, Provost of the College of Health Sciences. Professor Fred Stephen Sarfo, Provost of the College of Health Sciences, described the outreach as a practical expression of the University’s commitment to translating knowledge into meaningful community service. “Today is a very important day for the College of Health Sciences. We are gathered not simply to mark an anniversary, but to demonstrate what seventy-five years of KNUST should mean in practical terms: knowledge translated into service, professional expertise brought closer to the people, and stronger partnerships between the University and its neighbouring communities,” he stated. Prof. Sarfo said that while the College is dedicated to training health professionals, advancing research and improving health outcomes, those responsibilities must extend beyond lecture halls, laboratories and hospitals into the communities where people live and work. He said the choice of Anwomaso Market as the venue was deliberate because markets serve as important centres of economic and social activity, making healthcare services more accessible to surrounding communities. Prof. Sarfo also underscored the importance of teamwork among healthcare professionals, noting that effective healthcare delivery depends on collaboration among doctors, pharmacists, nurses, dentists, laboratory professionals, physiotherapists, optometrists, veterinary professionals, public health practitioners and students. “No single profession can meet all the health needs of a community,” he observed, adding that the outreach also provided students with valuable practical experience in interprofessional collaboration, communication and patient-centred care. Encouraging community members to participate actively, he advised residents to openly discuss their health concerns with healthcare providers and comply with referral recommendations where further assessment or treatment was required. Prof. Sarfo also stressed the importance of preventive healthcare, noting that many diseases can either be prevented or effectively managed through regular health checks, healthy lifestyles, appropriate medication use and early medical consultation. He expressed appreciation to the organising committee, faculty, students, volunteers, traditional leaders, assembly representatives, market leaders, community mobilisers and development partners whose contributions made the outreach possible. Calling on members of the outreach team to uphold the highest professional standards throughout the exercise, he urged them to safeguard patient dignity, confidentiality and safety while communicating clearly with participants. “The value of today’s programme will not be measured only by the number of people screened. It will also be measured by the quality of the interactions, the referrals completed, the knowledge shared and the trust strengthened between the College and the communities,” he said. He described the outreach as both a celebration of KNUST’s 75th anniversary and a reaffirmation of the College of Health Sciences’ commitment to remaining responsive to the healthcare needs of Ghanaians. Nana Akwasi Poku, Gyaasehene of Anwomaso, speaking on behalf of the Anwomasohene, Nana Osei Boah III, expressed appreciation to KNUST and the College of Health Sciences for bringing the outreach to the community, describing the initiative as a significant contribution to the health and well-being of residents. He thanked the University for “bringing healing, care and essential health services to the residents of this community,” noting that the outreach would benefit many people who might otherwise have limited access to such services. Nana Poku encouraged residents of Anwomaso and neighbouring communities to participate fully in the programme and take advantage of the free medical consultations, screening and health education being offered. He also expressed hope that the outreach would become a recurring initiative rather than a one-time event. “I hope that this will not be the only time such a programme is held here. We welcome more of these initiatives in the future to continue supporting the health and well-being of our people,” he said.

items.title: Majority leadership change ‘shocking’ – ACEPA’s boss
items.description: The Executive Director of the African Centre for Parliamentary Affairs (ACEPA), Dr Rasheed Draman, has described the anticipated change in Parliament’s Majority leadership as “shocking”, warning that frequent reshuffles involving senior parliamentary figures risk undermining the separation of powers and disrupting legislative business. Dr Draman made the remarks during an interview on Top Story on Joy FM, following the nomination of Majority Leader Mahama Ayariga as Minister-designate for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs by President John Dramani Mahama. Mr Ayariga’s nomination is expected to pave the way for Builsa North Member of Parliament James Agalga to assume the role of Majority Leader, pending the completion of the necessary parliamentary processes. Reacting to the development, Dr Draman said the move reflects a longstanding constitutional and governance concern over the close relationship between the Executive and the Legislature. “I think for me, it is shocking and that speaks to the issues that we have been talking about over the years, separation of power and the divorce of legislature from the executive.” According to him, abrupt changes in parliamentary leadership have historically affected the work of Parliament, with some legislative initiatives losing momentum whenever key leaders are reassigned to the Executive. “I have been following our Parliament for many, many years, and I know some legislative issues have suffered in the past when we have had this sudden kind of reshuffles.” Dr Draman said leadership continuity is important to sustaining parliamentary reforms and ensuring that ongoing legislative work is not interrupted by changes arising from Cabinet appointments. Despite expressing concern over the transition, he said he was hopeful that the work initiated by Mr Ayariga as Majority Leader would be sustained under his successor. “That is how it came to me, but I hope what Majority Leader Mahama Ayariga has started and has been championing over close to almost two years now will continue under the new leadership.”

items.title: Kankan prête pour la 5ᵉ édition de la West Africa Champions Cup : les organisateurs font le point avec les médias
items.description: À quelques jours du lancement officiel de la cinquième édition de la West Africa Champions Cup (WAC) 2026 à Kankan, les organisateurs ont animé une conférence de presse ce vendredi 7 août 2026 afin de présenter les grandes articulations de cette compétition qui réunit neuf clubs de la sous-région. Cette rencontre avec les médias a été marquée par les interventions des promoteurs Alpha Mady Touré et Cellou Tata Diallo, qui ont mis en lumière les objectifs du tournoi, les innovations de cette édition ainsi que les dispositions prises pour garantir son bon déroulement. Dans son intervention, le co-promoteur du tournoi, Cellou Tata Diallo, a précisé : « La compétition va réunir neuf clubs. Au départ, il y en avait dix, mais les Soudanais d'Al Hilal se sont finalement retirés au dernier moment, arguant du fait qu'il y a une forte pluviométrie en Guinée. Donc, ça ne permet pas d'avoir de bonnes conditions de préparation, même si on sait qu'à Kankan, il ne pleut pas trop. Donc, nous restons avec neuf clubs : les quatre clubs maliens, dont deux en Ligue des champions et deux en Coupe de la Confédération, un club sierra-léonais qui est en Ligue des champions, un club mauritanien, deux clubs guinéens, le Horoya et le Hafia, engagés respectivement en Ligue des champions et en Coupe de la Confédération, et puis il y a le Karfamoriah FC de Kankan, dont le président nous accompagne depuis plusieurs années. Au niveau des nouveautés, comme on l'a dit, c'est que la RTG accepte d'accompagner cette fois la compétition. On aura la possibilité, cette fois-ci, non pas de passer par Internet, mais de faire une diffusion par satellite. Donc, il y aura une réalisation multicaméra avec le ralenti et tout ce qu'il y a autour. L'autre nouveauté, c'est de garantir à chaque équipe trois matchs et puis, au bout, on verra les deux équipes les mieux classées jouer la finale. » Le secrétaire général de la Fédération Guinéenne de Football, Elhadj Ibrahima Blasco Barry, a salué cette initiative, qui contribue au développement du football ouest-africain et au renforcement des échanges entre les jeunes talents de la sous-région. « Permettez-moi, au nom de la Fédération Guinéenne de Football, de saluer cette belle initiative qui contribue au rayonnement du football guinéen et au renforcement de la coopération sportive entre les pays de notre sous-région. Je tiens à rendre un hommage appuyé aux promoteurs de cette compétition, Alpha Mady Touré et Cellou Tata Diallo, ainsi qu'à l'ensemble du comité d'organisation. Dans un contexte où les ressources sont souvent limitées, ils ont fait preuve d'une détermination remarquable, d'une résilience exemplaire et d'un engagement sans faille pour faire aboutir ce projet ambitieux », a déclaré le responsable de l'instance dirigeante du football guinéen. Présente à cette rencontre, la directrice générale de la Radio Télévision Guinéenne (RTG), Makeme Bamba, a réaffirmé l'engagement du média de service public, diffuseur officiel de cette 5ᵉ édition, à assurer une couverture médiatique de qualité afin de rapprocher les passionnés de football de cet événement majeur organisé à Kankan. À ce sujet, elle a déclaré : « Nous avons eu ce partenariat et nous avons dit : nous allons accompagner. Cet accompagnement va non seulement permettre le premier tournage avec ce nouveau car de reportage, mais aussi permettre à l'équipe de bien maîtriser les équipements qui se trouvent dans ce nouveau car afin de nous propulser et d'aller plus loin. Ne pas se contenter des matchs guinéens, mais aussi des matchs de la sous-région, pourquoi pas si le résultat est concluant. » Pendant neuf jours, du 14 au 22 août 2026, les passionnés de football vibreront au rythme des affiches opposant les neuf clubs engagés dans cette édition : Horoya AC, Hafia FC et Karfamoriah FC (Guinée), Stade Malien de Bamako, Djoliba AC, Réal de Bamako et FC Diarra (Mali), Star Sport Academy (Sierra Leone), ainsi que FC Zidan (Mauritanie), invité de prestige. Une compétition qui promet un spectacle de haut niveau et confirme l'ambition de la West Africa Champions Cup de s'imposer comme l'un des grands rendez-vous du football ouest-africain. items.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs2.20, high-speed diesel by Rs1.50
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · "> The government on Friday reduced the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.20 and Rs1.50 per litre, respectively. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs327.62 per litre while HSD will cost Rs380.86 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on HSD. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will apply from August 8 to 10. The diesel price has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

In a post sighted on his Instagram account, he wrote: “10 years of hits, memories, and timeless moments with you.” “Now the journey continues. My third studio album WHEREDOWEGOFROMHERE?#WDWGFH August 27th.” The post has been met with exciting reactions from fans who simply can’t wait to hear what KiDi has been working on for the last two years. In the coming days, the singer will reveal track titles on the album as well as regional and international features. Since 2024, the platinum artiste, promised his fans a third studio album after the successes of his previous projects which topped the charts and were adjudged ‘Album of the Year’. As part of the rollout for ‘WDWGFH’, the music icon is expected to embark on a number of promotional activities, including a listening session in London and Accra as well as an album release party. items.title: Trafic de motos volées à Conakry : un vaste réseau démantelé et plusieurs engins saisis
items.description: Les services spéciaux ont présenté à la presse, ce vendredi, onze hommes soupçonnés d'appartenir à un réseau spécialisé dans le vol, le recel et la revente de motos à Conakry. L'opération, menée à Mafanko, sur la Route du Niger, a permis la saisie de plusieurs engins dont les caractéristiques auraient été volontairement modifiées afin d'en dissimuler l'origine. Selon le commissaire principal de police Foromo Soropogui, en service à la Direction de lutte contre le crime organisé, l'enquête a été ouverte à la suite d'informations fournies par des sources jugées crédibles et confirmées par plusieurs recoupements. Ces renseignements faisaient état de l'existence d'un réseau opérant à partir d'un garage où exerçaient notamment des mécaniciens et des électriciens. « À la suite de dénonciations provenant de sources crédibles, recoupées par plusieurs autres informations, notre service a procédé, le 4 août 2026, à l'interpellation de onze personnes et à la saisie de plusieurs motos volées », a déclaré le responsable policier. D'après les enquêteurs, les motos dérobées étaient rapidement acheminées vers ce garage où elles faisaient l'objet de multiples transformations. Les membres présumés du réseau remplaçaient notamment le réservoir, le phare ou encore la selle, modifiaient l'apparence générale des engins et falsifiaient les numéros de châssis afin de rendre leur identification quasiment impossible. Le commissaire Soropogui affirme également que le réseau se procurait de fausses clés, de faux certificats d'immatriculation ainsi que des plaques d'immatriculation grâce à la complicité présumée de certains agents, avant d'écouler les motos sur le marché. Les personnes interpellées, âgées de 27 à 44 ans, sont : Sékou Camara, présenté comme le chef présumé du réseau, Mamady Cissé, Sayon Kaba, Idrissa Condé, Souleymane Traoré, Alya Camara, Sory Doumbouya, Oumar Sory Savané, Mahamed Lamine Bangoura, Abdoulaye Traoré et Ibrahima « Ilaye » Condé. Au cours de leurs auditions, les mis en cause ont rejeté les accusations portées contre eux. La police soutient toutefois que les motos saisies ne disposaient d'aucun document administratif et que leurs numéros de châssis avaient été falsifiés, des éléments qu'elle considère comme des indices sérieux de leur provenance frauduleuse. Parmi les suspects, Souleymane Traoré nie toute implication dans ce réseau et affirme n'avoir exercé que son activité de mécanicien. « Je ne fais pas partie de ce réseau. Je suis mécanicien. Lorsque des clients me confient une moto pour une réparation ou pour remplacer une pièce, je fais simplement mon travail. Je ne connais rien de cette affaire. Je travaille à Mafanko et je n'exerce que mon métier », s'est-il défendu devant les journalistes. Les onze suspects sont poursuivis pour association de malfaiteurs et vol aggravé, des infractions prévues et réprimées par les articles 784 et 374 du Code pénal, selon la police. Aux dernières nouvelles, ils devaient être déférés devant le tribunal de première instance de Mafanco, où la justice devra établir les responsabilités de chacun dans cette affaire.

items.title: Kaloum – Deux mois de prison pour le vol de 11 barres de fer au port de Conakry : « C’est la première fois que je vole »
items.description: Chauffeur de profession, Naby Laye Moussa Camara a été condamné à deux mois de prison par le tribunal correctionnel de Kaloum, ce jeudi 6 août 2026, pour vol de onze (11) barres de fer au port autonome de Conakry. Le prévenu était poursuivi par le parquet pour avoir soustrait ces barres de fer dans l’enceinte du port autonome de Conakry. Il était détenu à la maison centrale de Conakry depuis le 3 août dernier. Interrogé à la barre sur les faits qui lui sont reprochés, Naby Laye Moussa Camara a plaidé coupable. « Je suis chauffeur de camion au port autonome de Conakry. Je ne suis pas habitué à voler, c’est ma première fois de faire ça. Je demande pardon », a déclaré le prévenu. Dans ses réquisitions, le ministère public a requis deux mois de prison ferme contre le prévenu. Statuant publiquement et contradictoirement, le tribunal a déclaré Naby Laye Moussa Camara coupable des faits qui lui sont reprochés et l’a condamné à deux mois de prison. items.title: Pop Culture Has Its Teeth in You
items.description: In their fledgling but fascinating career thus far, the director Jane Schoenbrun has been consumed by the pop culture that consumes us. They’ve already proved to be an urgent voice on the matter: Their first feature, the low-budget We’re All Going to the World’s Fair , focused on the allure of online “creepypastas” and weird YouTube rabbit holes that despondent teenagers might go down. The second, I Saw the TV Glow , examined the psychological fallout of two isolated adolescents obsessed with a cult television series. Schoenbrun’s newest movie, Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma , is similarly interested in nostalgia: It follows Kris (played by Hannah Einbinder), a queer filmmaker tasked with rebooting a gruesome slasher franchise from yesteryear called Camp Miasma . As she does so, the past and the cynical present blend into a transfixing dilution of Schoenbrun’s interests and fears about identity and self through the prism of mass media. Schoenbrun’s previous films were intensely melancholic affairs, and it’s immediately clear that Camp Miasma is having a bit more fun with the same themes. It jabs at Hollywood’s impulse toward rampant intellectualization—and corporatization—of the cinematic junk food of decades past. Kris, who has a minor Sundance hit under her belt, endeavors to create a “woke” and hip take on Camp Miasma without alienating its enduring fan base. A charmingly stylized early montage establishes the franchise as akin to many 1980s VHS cult classics, garishly mixing gore, nudity, and an eerie campfire vibe. The film’s many sequels yielded diminishing returns, and the series eventually stooped to wacky concepts à la Friday the 13th —the main monster, Little Death, who carries a spear and wears a mask shaped like a cubic air vent, traveled to Manhattan, then space, and so on. At her hotel, Kris watches the original film and eagerly takes notes; during a cheesy sex scene, she scribbles DESIRE in her notepad and underlines it forcefully. Yet Kris, despite her intent to take a cerebral approach, also comes at the project with a teen sensibility. Any movie nerd might recognize her behavior: When she stops off at a gas station on a work trip, she grabs fistfuls of candy and then lazily spins through the cheapo DVD rack, excitedly calling a friend when she finds a junky Camp Miasma installment for sale. The opportunity to visit the now-abandoned sleepaway camp where the first entry was shot is both useful to her as a director and delightful to her as a fan. [ Read: Make culture weird again ] The film mostly takes place there, and Kris spends a bizarre weekend with Billy Presley (Gillian Anderson), a reclusive actor who starred in the original Camp Miasma but refused to participate in any of its follow-ups. Billy, however, now lives at the campground with the goal of giving herself what appears to be a peculiar form of exposure therapy. Anderson, herself a towering legend of genre television and cinema, is an imperiously fun and sexy figure for Einbinder’s nervous and dorky character to bounce off of. Billy seems both enticed and exhausted by Kris, who professes her struggle to bring an academic eye to the world of Camp Miasma . Billy reminds her that the franchise’s initial appeal was straightforward: The draw was “flesh and fluids.” As Kris spends more time with Billy, Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma metamorphoses from an industry satire into a dreamlike reflection on how what we watch can shape us, no matter how lowbrow. Schoenbrun renders the desolate grounds with beautiful matte-painted backgrounds; as Kris and Billy watch the old film, the fuzzy visuals and synthy score bleed away into contemporary CGI blood and carnage. Both the throwback and present-day imagery look surreal; even though Kris can identify the obvious tropes in Camp Miasma , she can’t seem to face the power that familiar scripts hold over her. And in a fantastical twist, Little Death somehow finds its way out of the Camp Miasma movies, emerging from the on-site lake. But this is not a tale of cinema coming to life and invading the mundane real world; it’s more about two different styles of storytelling blending into one. As past and present, “fiction” and “reality” swirl together for an inscrutable final act, Schoenbrun finds a fresh way to make an incisive observation about 21st-century life: Today’s moviegoers are immersed in their screens and hungry for pop culture, to the point that a trashy flick such as Camp Miasma can feel intrinsic to Kris’s sense of self. Someone like Kris may want to interrogate that relationship over and over in search of meaning, but perhaps it’s best not to subject what we watch to endless analysis and meta-critique. Instead, we may be better off embracing how we feel.

items.title: Africa Golf Tourism Convention 2026 reveals speakers for inaugural Ekurhuleni gathering in South Africa
items.description: Organisers of the inaugural Africa Golf Tourism Convention (AGTC) 2026 have unveiled the first batch of speakers expected to headline the landmark event scheduled for Ekurhuleni, Gauteng, South Africa. The four-day convention, set for August 18 to 21, 2026, aims to create a unified marketplace connecting Africa’s golf, tourism, hospitality and trade sectors while positioning the continent as a competitive destination for high-value sports tourism. The speaker line-up brings together senior public officials, tourism executives, hospitality professionals, business leaders and sports personalities from across Africa and beyond. Among those confirmed are Acting Chief Executive Officer of the Gauteng Tourism Authority, Crezelda Venter; Chief Destination Marketing Evangelist at Visit Gauteng, Barba Gaoganediwe; Head of the Gauteng Convention & Event Bureau, Nonnie Kubeka; and Global President of Circle of Global Business Women, Dr Sindiswa Mzamo. The convention will also feature commercial and international voices including Peter Tshidi, Director of Medium and Small Properties at Sun International; António Louro, Executive Director of Mangais Golf Resort in Angola; Joaquin Valverde, General Manager of the Spanish Chamber of Commerce South Africa; and Sadiq Dindar, Founder of AfriLuxe Tourism Advisory Services. Other speakers include Gauteng Tour Operators Association President Victor Sibeko, Founder and President of the Chamber of Business and Tourism Dr Tebogo Mokope Modjadji, television sports presenter OG Molefe, golf lifestyle entrepreneur Innocentia Motau and wellness advocate Sonia Booth. Founder and Convention Director of AGTC, Neo Peete, said the selected speakers reflect the convention’s ambition to provide strategic insights into Africa’s tourism and hospitality landscape. “Our objective from inception was to assemble a faculty of genuine change-makers who possess deep operational and strategic insights into Africa’s tourism, trade and hospitality dynamics,” she said. Neo Peete added that the event would provide delegates and exhibitors with practical approaches to developing sports tourism assets, expanding cross-border trade and creating new commercial opportunities. Co-founder and Exhibitions Director of AGTC, Gisele Masengo, said the convention provides a platform for tourism operators and golf-related businesses to connect directly with international buyers. “Africa represents one of the most promising frontiers for luxury sports travel, yet sellers of golf and tourism products have lacked a dedicated platform to present their offerings directly to qualified buyers,” she said. She encouraged destination management companies, hotel groups, golf resorts and sports apparel brands to register for exhibition spaces and trade passes. The first three days of AGTC 2026 will feature keynote sessions, business-to-business meetings, destination showcases, exhibitions and networking engagements involving tourism authorities, airlines, investors, golf industry leaders and international media. The convention will conclude with a championship golf day at Serengeti Estate, one of South Africa’s leading golfing destinations, where delegates will experience the link between golf, hospitality and business tourism. Organisers say the event is expected to strengthen Africa’s participation in the global golf tourism economy while creating new partnerships across the continent’s travel and leisure sectors.

items.title: Le CLO Doufelgou évalue la campagne de distribution de moustiquaires
items.description: Niamtougou, 7 août (ATOP) – Le Comité local d’organisation (CLO) de la campagne de distribution gratuite de Moustiquaires imprégnées d’insecticide (MII) du district sanitaire de Doufelgou a tenu, le vendredi 7 août à Niamtougou, une réunion d’évaluation post-distribution. Cette rencontre a permis de faire le bilan des opérations et d’apprécier les résultats obtenus. Elle a servi également de cadre pour identifier les difficultés rencontrées sur le terrain et de définir des stratégies destinées à renforcer la sensibilisation des populations en vue d’une utilisation régulière et correcte des moustiquaires distribuées. Les participants ​Les échanges ont révélé que la campagne s’est déroulée de manière globalement satisfaisante grâce à la mobilisation des différents acteurs. Toutefois, quelques difficultés ont été signalées par les équipes de suivi. Il s’agit notamment de l’absence de certains ménages recensés sur les sites de distribution, de l’impossibilité pour les responsables de formations sanitaires de joindre plusieurs chefs de famille par téléphone. Pour faire face à ces contraintes, les membres du comité ont recommandé le renforcement du suivi de proximité ainsi que la poursuite des actions de sensibilisation et de communication communautaire afin d’encourager l’utilisation quotidienne et correcte des MII, moyen efficace de prévention du paludisme. La présentation des opérations Le directeur préfectoral de la Santé de Doufelgou, Dr Alassani Nourou, a rappelé que la possession d’une moustiquaire ne suffit pas à elle seule à prévenir le paludisme. Selon lui, seule son utilisation effective et quotidienne permet aux populations de se protéger. Il a indiqué que les équipes sanitaires intensifieront les activités de sensibilisation de proximité et les visites à domicile afin de s’assurer que les MII reçues sont effectivement installées et utilisées au-dessus des couchages. Le préfet de Doufelgou, Colonel Aziaba Ayi Sessi, président du CLO, a estimé que les difficultés relevées ne remettent pas en cause les résultats de la campagne. Il a invité les membres du comité à maintenir le contact avec les ménages absents afin d’organiser des séances de rattrapage pour leur permettre de retirer leurs moustiquaires. ATOP/SG/TAL/BA

items.title: The Republic where Heroes Die while Villains Keep Digging…
items.description: On that August morning, eight Ghanaians boarded a Ghana Armed Forces helicopter expecting, like countless public servants before them, to complete another official assignment and return home before nightfall. They never did. Instead, the Republic lowered its flags. For a few solemn days, Ghana forgot its political quarrels. Radio stations softened their voices. Television presenters abandoned their usual excitement. Across the country, families mourned with families they had never met, because death has a remarkable way of reminding us that before we become NPP or NDC, ministers or soldiers, we are first fathers, husbands, brothers and friends. The men aboard that helicopter were travelling to Obuasi as part of Ghana’s continuing struggle against illegal mining. It was a journey undertaken in the service of the Republic. They paid the ultimate price. Months passed. The funerals ended. The flags were raised again. As often happens in Ghana, the headlines moved on. Then President John Mahama made a remarkable admission. Speaking about galamsey, he openly acknowledged that even members of his own political family were involved in the very enterprise his government was trying to defeat. He went further, observing that whenever governments change, many of those involved simply change political colours and continue with business as usual. It was one of those rare moments when a politician merely confirmed what the rivers have been whispering for years. Perhaps that explains why Ghana’s war against galamsey has become one of the strangest wars ever fought. Every new government arrives with bigger promises than the one before it. New task forces are inaugurated. Fresh operations are launched. Excavators are seized before television cameras. Opposition parties diagnose government failures with the confidence of Korle Bu specialists discussing somebody else’s patient. The Republic applauds. Then we quietly walk to the nearest river. The river clears its throat and delivers a different verdict. There is one institution in Ghana that no government has ever succeeded in capturing. The rivers. They have stubbornly refused to become state agencies. They do not attend ministerial briefings, applaud presidential launches or adjust their colours to suit election results. The Pra, the Birim and the Ankobra continue behaving like incorruptible public auditors, quietly examining every administration and publishing their reports in shades of brown. Rivers, it seems, are among the very few institutions in the Republic that cannot be transferred, intimidated or bribed. That is why the President’s confession deserves more than applause for honesty. If governments already know that some of their own supporters are involved in destroying our rivers, then our greatest challenge is no longer discovering the criminals. It is finding the courage to confront them. Our elders solved this puzzle long ago. They warned that anyone who spends every evening killing mosquitoes while refusing to drain the stagnant water behind the house should prepare to spend a fortune on mosquito coils. The Republic has become remarkably skilled at buying mosquito coils. We chase the young man standing waist-deep in muddy water while politely avoiding the powerful financier who purchased the excavator. We arrest the labourer but hesitate whenever the trail begins leading towards influence, wealth or political usefulness. We prune the branches with admirable enthusiasm while carefully watering the roots. That is why this debate should never become another football match between the NPP and the NDC. The previous government failed to defeat galamsey. The present government spent years explaining exactly why that failure occurred. It therefore inherited not only the responsibility of governing but also the responsibility of proving that its own diagnosis was correct. And perhaps that is the saddest lesson hidden inside that helicopter crash. A Republic should never ask its bravest citizens to risk their lives pursuing people it already knows but still struggles to confront. The greatest tribute we can pay those eight patriots is not another beautifully organised memorial service. It is ensuring that they did not sacrifice their lives merely to become another chapter in Ghana’s endless catalogue of noble intentions. History will remember the soldiers. History will remember the ministers. History will remember the public servants who never came home. The Republic must now decide whether it also wishes to remember why they boarded that helicopter. For there can be no sadder epitaph for any nation than this: Here lies a Republic where heroes died… while the villains simply kept digging. What do you think is Ghana’s biggest obstacle in defeating galamsey: political interference, corruption, poverty, weak law enforcement, or something else entirely? #StopGalamsey #SaveOurRivers #RepublicOfUncommonSense #Ghana

items.title: Lutte contre la mortalité maternelle: La SOGOB forme les sages-femmes à la prévention de l’hémorragie du post-partum
items.description: La Société des gynécologues et obstétriciens du Burkina (SOGOB) a organisé, les 6 et 7 août 2026 à Tenkodogo, un atelier de renforcement des capacités au profit des sages-femmes afin de lutter contre l’hémorragie du post-partum (HPP), l’une des principales causes de mortalité maternelle. Au Burkina Faso, environ 30 % des décès maternels sont dus à l’hémorragie du post-partum (HPP), ce qui en fait l’une des principales causes de mortalité maternelle. À travers le renforcement des capacités des acteurs de santé, la SOGOB apporte son soutien aux efforts du gouvernement en faveur de l’amélioration de la santé maternelle. Cet engagement se traduit notamment par l’adoption et la mise en œuvre de politiques ambitieuses, telles que la gratuité des soins de santé maternelle et de la planification familiale, ainsi que l’activation récente du Centre des opérations de réponse aux urgences sanitaires (CORUS), qui classe désormais les décès maternels parmi les incidents de santé, renforçant ainsi leur surveillance et la riposte. Le taux de mortalité maternelle au Burkina Faso est estimé à 198 décès pour 100 000 naissances vivantes, un niveau encore éloigné de la cible fixée par les Objectifs de développement durable (ODD), qui est de moins de 70 décès pour 100 000 naissances vivantes. Selon l’animateur de l’atelier, Pr Yobi Alexis Sawadogo, accélérer la réduction de la mortalité maternelle constitue un impératif si le Burkina Faso veut atteindre les Objectifs de développement durable. Pour y parvenir, le rôle des sage-femmes est essentiel, d’autant plus que la sensibilisation du grand public et des décideurs demeure insuffisante. Pr Yobi Alexis Sawadogo « Les sage-femmes, en tant que relais d’opinion, jouent un rôle stratégique dans la diffusion des messages de plaidoyer et la mobilisation sociale autour de cette problématique. C’est dans ce cadre que la Société des gynécologues et obstétriciens du Burkina (SOGOB) renforce leurs capacités afin d’améliorer la mobilisation communautaire et sociale autour de cette problématique », a indiqué le Pr Yobi. Durant les deux jours de formation, une trentaine de sage-femmes ont renforcé leurs capacités en matière de plaidoyer pour la réduction de la mortalité maternelle liée à l’HPP, dans le but de favoriser une meilleure couverture médiatique et une mobilisation citoyenne plus efficace. Les participantes ont également échangé sur la situation de la mortalité maternelle et de l’hémorragie du post-partum dans le monde et au Burkina Faso. À l’issue de l’atelier, les sage-femmes ont été invitées à poursuivre leur engagement dans la lutte contre l’hémorragie du post-partum, en particulier, et plus largement contre la mortalité maternelle au Burkina Faso. B.S.

items.title: Why Tinubu will win in 2027 — Accord presidential candidate
items.description: Prof. Christopher Imumolen, the factional Accord Party’s presidential candidate and National Chairman, says President Bola Tinubu is well positioned to win the 2027 presidential election because of his reforms, leadership and growing nationwide support. Imumolen stated this at a news conference in Lagos on Friday, where he formally announced his withdrawal from the 2027 presidential race and endorsed Tinubu for a second term. He said the decision followed extensive consultations with the party’s leadership and members. Imumolen said that national interest should always take precedence over personal ambition and partisan considerations. According to him, Tinubu’s re-election is inevitable because Nigerians are beginning to appreciate the long-term benefits of the administration’s reform agenda despite prevailing economic challenges. “Tinubu will win because of his people-oriented programmes and the massive support he has received from different parts of the country. “There is focus. Let us forget about the challenges of inflation and security. There must be progress “If another person comes in 2027,he will have to start all over again. “There must be continuity. He has identified the challenges, and we need to move from where we are to the next phase. That is why we are supporting him, and he will win. My support is total,” Imumolen said. He said the President’s reform agenda closely aligned with his own manifesto, especially in economic transformation, education, youth empowerment, entrepreneurship, industrialisation and national development. Imumolen said the party endorsed him for ten reasons and after reviewing the administration’s performance and Nigeria’s future development needs He said the first three reasons were Tinubu’s courage in implementing difficult economic reforms, demonstrated leadership capacity and commitment to progressive governance through continuity of development projects. According to him, the fourth, fifth and sixth reasons were deliberate youth empowerment, bridging generational leadership and appointing competent individuals into strategic public offices. He said the seventh, eighth and ninth reasons were placing national interest above personal ambition, ensuring policy continuity, political stability and sustained reforms, and demonstrating transparency through the party’s early endorsement. Imumolen said the tenth reason was the party’s conviction that collaboration in the national interest would strengthen democracy and accelerate national development. “Over the last four years, I was one of those who criticised the President. However, I have also witnessed his leadership style and the progress his administration has made,” he said. He said no opposition presidential candidate, including those of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and National Democratic Congress (NDC), possessed a stronger prospect than Tinubu. According to him, the appointments have created opportunities for young people to contribute meaningfully to governance and national development. Imumolen commended the administration for appointing young Nigerians into strategic positions, saying the President had demonstrated confidence in the country’s younger generation. “I believe President Bola Tinubu is uniquely positioned to provide a seamless transition between Nigeria’s founding democratic leadership and the emerging generation of transformational leaders,” he said. Imumolen reiterated that his political aspiration had always been driven by service to Nigeria rather than the pursuit of public office. “My aspiration has always been to serve Nigeria and not merely to occupy political office. “Whenever the national interest is better served through unity and strategic collaboration, I will always choose Nigeria above personal interest,” he said. He said continuity in governance remained essential for attracting investment, creating jobs, strengthening institutions and sustaining ongoing reforms across the country. “These are some of the reasons our party has collectively resolved to stand behind President Tinubu in the forthcoming election. “There is no hidden agenda. Our only objective is to support what we believe is good for Nigeria and secure a better future for ourselves and our children,” he said. Imumolen said the party announced its endorsement ahead of the election to demonstrate openness and provide clarity to its members and supporters. He dismissed claims that the endorsement resulted from weak political structures, insisting the decision was based entirely on performance and national interest. “Our party evaluates leaders based on their performance. We have assessed Mr President’s record and believe supporting him is in the national interest,” he said. Imumolen explained that the party deliberately declined to field a presidential candidate because it believed continuity would consolidate the reforms initiated by the Tinubu administration. He assured supporters that the presidential endorsement would not affect Accord Party’s participation in governorship, legislative and other elections across the country. items.title: Montée mensuelle des grandes couleurs : Le Manifeste de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire remis aux élèves
items.description: L'École nationale de police (ENP) a organisé, ce vendredi 7 août 2026, la traditionnelle cérémonie de montée des grandes couleurs, un moment de communion patriotique et de réaffirmation de l'engagement collectif au service de la Nation. ‎ ‎La cérémonie a été présidée par le Camarade Directeur général de l'École nationale de police, le Commissaire divisionnaire de police Abdoulaye BELEM, en présence du personnel administratif et d'encadrement, ainsi que des élèves de la 56ᵉ promotion en formation. ‎ ‎Dans son adresse, le Camarade Directeur général a salué les efforts consentis par l'ensemble du personnel dans l'accomplissement des missions assignées à l'École. Il a félicité chacun pour les résultats enregistrés et a exhorté les différents services à maintenir cette dynamique de performance, de rigueur et de professionnalisme afin de consolider davantage le rayonnement de l'école mère de la Police nationale. ‎ ‎S'inscrivant dans la vision portée par les plus hautes autorités de notre pays, le Camarade Directeur général a procédé à la remise du Manifeste de la Révolution progressiste populaire aux élèves de la 56ᵉ promotion. Il a annoncé que cet ouvrage sera également mis, dans les prochains jours, à la disposition de l'ensemble du personnel de l'École. ‎ ‎À cette occasion, il a invité le personnel et les élèves à épouser pleinement les idéaux de la Révolution progressiste populaire, fondés sur le patriotisme, l'intégrité, le sens du sacrifice, la probité, la discipline, la souveraineté nationale et le service désintéressé pour la Patrie. Il a rappelé que chaque agent de l'ENP est appelé, par son comportement et son engagement, à contribuer activement à l'édification d'une administration exemplaire au service du Burkina Faso. ‎ ‎À travers cette cérémonie, l'École nationale de police réaffirme son attachement aux valeurs de patriotisme, de discipline, de mérite et d'excellence, qui constituent le socle de la formation des femmes et des hommes appelés à assurer la sécurité des populations et la défense des institutions de la République. ‎ ‎Bien apprendre pour mieux protéger !

items.title: Nigeria, China seal media, film pact to deepen cultural cooperation
items.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja Nigeria and the People’s Republic of China have strengthened their cultural cooperation with the signing of a Content Exchange and Cooperation Agreement between the China Movie Channel (CMC) and the Nigerian Television Authority (NTA). The agreement was signed during the China–Nigeria Film and Literature Symposium on Friday in Abuja. Speaking at the event, Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria, Yu Dunhai, highlighted the deep cultural and literary heritage shared by both nations. He said renowned Nigerian writers such as Wole Soyinka, Chinua Achebe, and Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie, alongside Chinese authors Mo Yan, Yu Hua, and Mai Jia, have played significant roles in promoting understanding between the peoples of both countries. The ambassador noted that Nigeria and China are global forces in visual storytelling and creative expression. According to him, China has more than 93,000 cinema screens and produces about 700 films annually, while Nigeria’s film industry releases over 2,000 films each year. He pointed to the positive reception of Chinese films such as My People, My Country in Nigeria and Nigerian productions including Lionheart and October 1st in China as proof of growing cultural appreciation between audiences in both nations. “The mutual appreciation of literature and film between the peoples of China and Nigeria is rooted in close friendship and cultural ties,” Ambassador Yu said, adding that the initiative aligns with Chinese President Xi Jinping’s Global Civilization Initiative and President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s commitment to strengthening cross-border cultural connections. He further noted that the agreement coincides with the 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations between China and Nigeria, the China-Africa Year of People-to-People Exchanges, and the 105th anniversary of the Communist Party of China (CPC). Representing the Nigerian government, Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy, Abdulkarim Ibrahim, described the agreement as a major boost for Nigeria’s creative and digital media sectors. He also acknowledged China’s continued support through fully funded educational, technical, and capacity-building programmes that have benefited many Nigerian public servants and creative industry professionals. Ibrahim said that as Nigeria pursues policies aimed at using the creative economy to drive employment and economic growth, partnerships such as this provide valuable technical expertise and support. According to him, “This partnership will create new opportunities for professional development, technological innovation, and co-productions,” Ibrahim said. Also speaking, Director-General of the Nigerian Television Authority (NTA), Salihu Abdulhamid Dembos, highlighted the practical benefits of the collaboration. He said the agreement would expand access to content and could introduce AI-powered translation tools, enabling audiences in both countries to engage more easily with each other’s television programming and film productions. The symposium ended with joint panel discussions involving Nigerian and Chinese filmmakers, authors, and media professionals, with participants exploring opportunities for future co-productions, knowledge sharing, and talent exchange programmes. The post Nigeria, China seal media, film pact to deepen cultural cooperation appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Chauffeurs de taxi condamnés à Tétouan : la justice réfute la thèse des "boucs émissaires"
items.description: La polémique suscitée par la condamnation de plusieurs chauffeurs de taxi à Tétouan, dans le sillage des événements migratoires vers Sebta, et avançant la thèse des « boucs émissaires », a été déconstruite par une source judiciaire qui assure que les décisions rendues par le tribunal de première instance reposent sur des éléments propres à chaque dossier et non sur la seule activité de transport. Il convient, selon cette source qui s'est confiée à Hespress , de distinguer le débat public sur la crise migratoire et les questions politiques qu'elle soulève de la responsabilité pénale individuelle, que les juridictions apprécient exclusivement à partir des faits établis et des preuves versées au dossier. Contrairement à ce qui a été avancé dans certains commentaires, les deux affaires jugées ne concernent pas des chauffeurs ayant simplement conduit des voyageurs vers Fnideq. Les enquêtes et les débats devant le tribunal auraient mis en évidence que les intéressés savaient que leurs passagers se rendaient dans la zone frontalière dans le but de tenter une migration irrégulière et qu'ils avaient contribué à faciliter cette démarche. Le premier dossier concerne un chauffeur de grand taxi assurant la liaison Tétouan-Fnideq. D'après les éléments retenus par la justice, il avait transporté sept personnes contre 20 dirhams chacune et dissimulé ses deux fils dans le coffre du véhicule. Il aurait reconnu que le trajet visait à permettre aux passagers de rejoindre la frontière en vue d'une tentative de passage vers Ceuta. La seconde affaire porte sur deux chauffeurs opérant sur les lignes Chefchaouen-Tétouan et Tétouan-Fnideq. Ils auraient admis avoir acheminé des personnes dont ils connaissaient l'intention de rejoindre la frontière pour tenter une migration clandestine, avant de les déposer à proximité de la sortie d'autoroute menant à Fnideq. La même source rappelle que le droit marocain n'impose pas aux chauffeurs de taxi de vérifier les intentions de leurs clients ni d'exercer un rôle de police judiciaire. Le transport de personnes entre différentes villes demeure parfaitement légal et la liberté de circulation est garantie. En revanche, relève-t-elle, la responsabilité pénale peut être engagée lorsqu'il est établi que le transporteur avait connaissance de l'objectif illicite du déplacement et qu'il y a volontairement apporté son concours. Autrement dit, souligne la source, la justice n'a pas sanctionné le fait de conduire des passagers à Fnideq, mais a examiné si les chauffeurs avaient sciemment facilité une tentative de migration irrégulière. C'est cette distinction qui, selon elle, sépare une activité professionnelle licite d'une participation à une infraction pénale. La source judiciaire réfute également l'idée selon laquelle les chauffeurs auraient été condamnés en raison de leur profession. Elle insiste sur le fait que chaque décision repose sur des faits individualisés, tout en rappelant que les personnes condamnées conservent le droit de contester les preuves et la qualification juridique devant les juridictions d'appel. Enfin, elle souligne que les jugements rendus ne visent pas à établir les responsabilités globales dans les événements de Ceuta, mais uniquement à statuer sur les responsabilités pénales individuelles des personnes poursuivies, conformément aux règles de procédure et aux éléments examinés par le tribunal. Organisée sous l'égide du ministère des Affaires culturelles en partenariat avec le Centre national du cinéma et de l'image (CNCI). Cette manifestation se veut, durant trois jours, un rendez-vous culturel et cinématographique ouvert sur la mer, alliant art, divertissement et sensibilisation dans un espace résolument familial. Cette manifestation fait du cinéma un langage du dialogue et une fenêtre ouverte sur la réflexion. Elle met en lumière des enjeux d’actualité qui touchent l’être humain et son environnement, notamment l’importance de la préservation du milieu marin ainsi que la sensibilisation aux dangers de la migration irrégulière et aux drames et conséquences sociales et humaines qu’elle engendre. Durant trois jours, la plage de la falaise à Monastir se transformera en un espace dédié au cinéma, aux échanges, aux activités culturelles et récréatives, ainsi qu’à la rencontre entre familles et jeunes, dans une expérience qui conjugue le plaisir du spectacle et la portée du message… Là où le cinéma rencontre le bleu de la mer, la culture devient un espace de vie et d’espoir. items.title: 'Historic day': Experts, politicos weigh in on Makkah defence pact
items.description: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Friday signed a joint defence pact in Makkah that empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them. The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, which seeks to strengthen the collective security of the three states, was signed by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Saudi Crown Prince and PM Mohammad bin Salman, and Turkiye’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan at the “Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence” held at Al-Safa Palace. Since the signing, experts, political figures and commentators have offered their views on the agreement, with many describing it as a significant regional development and a historic moment for the three countries. ‘Historic day’: Attaullah Tarar Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, while talking to a private TV channel, described the signing of the joint defence agreement between the three states as a “historic day” for Pakistan, saying the pact reflected growing recognition of the country’s defence capabilities and strengthened ties among the three nations. Speaking about the agreement, Tarar said the defence cooperation framework would take relations between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye to a new level. He credited Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir with bringing the three countries together, saying they had an “ideal working relationship” and that their teamwork had contributed to recent successes. An important milestone in defence cooperation: Saudi FM Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan said the pact underscored the depth of the fraternal and strategic relations between the three countries. He said the agreement marked an important milestone in their defence cooperation and embodied the three countries’ shared political will to safeguard security, support a more secure regional environment and pave the way for greater development and prosperity. ‘A good omen for the Muslim Ummah’: ex-minister Former federal minister Khawaja Saad Rafique took to X and hailed the agreement as “a historic development and a good omen for the Muslim Ummah”. “This agreement will prove to be a fundamental pillar for the stability, security and promotion of mutual brotherhood of the Ummah,” he wrote, praising the foresight of the three nations. ‘Welcome and timely development’ Former federal minister Mushahid Hussain called the agreement a “welcome and timely development at a crucial moment of turbulence and transformation”. In a post on X, he noted that the Makkah Agreement came soon after Pakistan’s pivotal role in brokering the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding between Iran and the US, as well as the launch of the Regional 4 Diplomatic Coordination Mechanism comprising Pakistan, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Egypt. “Today’s pact has a three-fold significance. This is the first Pan-Islamic military institutional initiative among three key Muslim countries, independent of the West,” he wrote. “Second, this Muslim Defence Pact is [a] big blow to Israel and [the] ‘Abraham Accords’, as it would be an effective counter to Israeli expansionism,” Hussain added. “Third, it’s good for Pakistan’s security, given the emerging India-Israeli Axis, which has [the] backing of some regional regimes as well.” A shift beyond the US Andreas Krieg of King’s College London said the deal showed a clear desire to diversify alliances beyond the United States. “Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan are not trying to replace the United States. They are building the capacity to protect their interests when Washington cannot or will not do so.” Riyadh, in particular, he said, “wants several layers of security rather than one American umbrella”, after the shock of the Iran war. The deal will support Saudi Arabia’s ambitions to become an organiser of regional security and diversify its defence umbrella, while Turkey and Pakistan gain political clout and access to potential Saudi investments, he said. Step towards regional security architecture Ilhan Naz, the author of Old World Empires , took to X and called the agreement, “A positive development & another step towards a regionally owned and operated security architecture.” Culmination of regional efforts already underway Burcu Ozcelik, a Senior Fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (Rusi), called the pact the product of ongoing regional efforts and cautioned against reading into it as “evidence of a post-American Middle East”. “If anything, it fits the broader US preference for greater regional burden-sharing, regional powers assuming more responsibility for deterrence and security while remaining embedded, to different degrees, within a US-centred security architecture,” she wrote on X. “This is the culmination of regional efforts already underway. Saudi Arabia and Pakistan already have a mutual defence agreement, while Ankara, Riyadh and Islamabad have spent months discussing a trilateral framework,” Ozcelik added. She noted that the signatories have their own sets of interests, priorities and existing commitments and that the agreement demonstrates a common direction. Still, the deal does not mean “unanimous consensus on all regional challenges or how to resolve them”.

items.title: GCB Bank appointed to committees for Ghana’s participation in global trade exhibitions
items.description: GCB Bank has been appointed to the National Planning Committee and several technical sub-committees overseeing Ghana’s participation in the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE) 2026. The appointments, made by the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, relate to Ghana’s preparations for the international trade and investment exhibition. Under the arrangement, the Bank will chair the Budget and Fundraising Committee, co-chair the Marketing and Publicity Committee, and serve as a member of the Business and Investment Committee. According to the Ministry, the appointments were based on GCB Bank’s experience in supporting Ghana-China trade, exporter development, stakeholder engagement and previous national trade initiatives. In a related development, the Bank has nominated Aurelia Baaba Ofori Odame, Head of its State-Owned Enterprises and Afro-Asia Banking Department, to represent it on the National Planning Committee for Ghana’s participation in the China International Import Expo 2026, the Specialised World Expo 2027 in Belgrade, Serbia, and the Green X Expo 2027 in Yokohama, Japan. The committees are expected to coordinate Ghana’s participation in the exhibitions, which are aimed at promoting trade, investment and international business partnerships. Commenting on the appointments, Ms Ofori Odame said they reflected the Bank’s commitment to supporting Ghana’s international trade objectives. “We are honoured by the confidence the Ministry has reposed in GCB Bank. These appointments affirm our commitment to facilitating cross-border trade and creating opportunities for Ghanaian businesses to access international markets. Through our specialised Afro-Asia Banking Department, we have consistently worked to connect businesses with strategic markets, particularly in Asia, and we look forward to contributing to Ghana’s participation in these global platforms,” she said. She added that international exhibitions such as the China International Import Expo and the World Expo provide opportunities for Ghanaian businesses to engage with buyers, investors and strategic partners while expanding their presence in international markets. GCB Bank says it has expanded its support for international trade in recent years through its Africa and Asia Corridor strategy by providing financial services, facilitating business partnerships and supporting exporters seeking access to regional and international markets.
