items.title: Spear Institute calls for overhaul of Ghana’s flood management system to prevent recurring disasters
items.description: Spear Institute has called for a major overhaul of Ghana’s flood management approach, urging authorities to shift from responding to disasters after they occur to investing in long-term prevention and climate resilience. The research firm made the call during a virtual media briefing on Friday, August 7, 2026, where it examined the country’s recurring flood crisis and proposed measures to reduce its impact. The session, themed “Flooding in Ghana: Paddling to Safety or Avoiding a Repeat,” analysed the causes and consequences of flooding through four areas: socioeconomic conditions, governance, engineering and infrastructure, and project management. According to Spear Institute, flooding has been a recurring challenge in Ghana for decades, but the growing impact on lives, businesses, infrastructure and livelihoods requires a more coordinated national response. Using the June 29, 2026 floods in Accra as a case study, the institute said the disaster exposed weaknesses in drainage systems, land-use planning and disaster preparedness. It said the floods led to major disruptions, including impassable roads, flooded homes and businesses, and interruptions to transport and commercial activities. The institute reported that more than 12 people lost their lives, seven were missing, and 7,761 households were displaced across 18 affected assemblies following the incident. Spear Institute identified climate change, rapid urbanisation and the destruction of natural flood-control systems such as wetlands as key factors worsening the impact and frequency of floods. It noted that increasing population growth and unplanned development are placing additional pressure on vulnerable areas. The research firm stressed that flooding is a complex challenge that cannot be addressed by one sector alone, requiring coordinated action across government, communities and private stakeholders. On the social and economic dimensions of flooding, Spear Institute said poverty and inequality often increase exposure to flood risks. It explained that some low-income households occupy flood-prone areas due to limited access to affordable and safer housing options. The institute also warned that households and small businesses without insurance, savings or access to credit often struggle to recover after losing property, equipment and sources of income. While identifying indiscriminate waste disposal as a contributor to blocked drains and waterways, the institute cautioned against placing the entire responsibility on citizens. It called for stronger waste management systems, including reliable collection services, accessible disposal facilities, enforcement and sustained public education. Spear Institute’s engineering and infrastructure team argued that Accra’s drainage systems must be reassessed and redesigned to reflect current population levels, urban expansion and changing rainfall patterns. It said the city recorded about 169.23 millimetres of rainfall during the June 29 floods, a volume that exceeded the capacity of some existing drainage infrastructure. The institute noted that several drains, culverts and bridges were constructed decades ago and no longer adequately serve today’s urban environment. It also raised concerns about the narrowing of waterways, including the Koli Lagoon and Odora River, due to encroachment, land reclamation and waste disposal. “When water loses its path, it creates another path,” one of the presenters said, highlighting the consequences of obstructed waterways. The institute further called for improved waste management, arguing that investments in drainage infrastructure would have limited impact if drains remain clogged with waste. Spear Institute also criticised weaknesses in project management, including inadequate attention to sustainability, quality control and stakeholder involvement. It argued that infrastructure projects should not be judged only by whether they are completed on time and within budget. Instead, projects must also be assessed on their ability to withstand future climate conditions and protect communities over time. The research firm criticised Ghana’s largely reactive approach to flooding, citing emergency interventions such as relief funding and nationwide de-silting exercises as responses that come after disasters occur. While acknowledging the importance of such interventions, Spear Institute said they do not address the underlying causes of flooding. It is calling for greater investment in proactive measures, including improved urban planning, restoration of wetlands, sustainable drainage systems and stronger flood-resilience strategies. The institute believes Ghana’s flood challenge requires an integrated national approach that combines engineering solutions with social protection, effective governance and better project management. It said the goal should be to develop systems capable of withstanding changing environmental conditions rather than repeatedly responding after floods strike. For Ghana, Spear Institute argues, the priority must now move from managing the aftermath of floods to preparing communities and cities before the next rainfall disaster occurs.

items.title: DPBEP 2027- 2029 : une consolidation budgétaire résolue, sans austérité
items.description: Le retour à la soutenabilité des finances publiques constitue le fil conducteur du Document de Programmation budgétaire et économique pluriannuelle (DPBEP) 2027- 2029. Le gouvernement inscrit le déficit dans une trajectoire de réduction continue : 4,9% du PIB en 2027, 3,8% en 2028, puis 3,0% en 2029, conformément à la norme communautaire de l'Union économique et monétaire ouest africaine (UEMOA). Le Document de Programmation budgétaire et économique pluriannuelle (DPBEP) 2027- 2029 montre que sur l'ensemble du triennat, les recettes de la loi de finances atteignent 19 228 milliards FCFA et les dépenses 22 133 milliards. Pour les recettes du budget général, elles progressant de 716 milliards quand les dépenses ne s'accroissent que de 350 milliards. A lire aussi : Finances publiques : les recettes de l’État estimées à 427,9 milliards de FCFA en mai 2026 « Cet ajustement repose sur une logique claire : rationaliser ce qui ne transforme pas, investir dans ce qui transforme. Les dépenses courantes reculent de 159 milliards FCFA sur la période, à la faveur de la maîtrise de la masse salariale, dont le ratio sur les recettes fiscales demeure sous le seuil de 35%, et de la rationalisation des subventions et transferts au secteur parapublic », indique le document. Dans le même temps, souligne la même source, les dépenses d'investissement progressent de 510 milliards FCFA, orientées vers les projets à fort impact économique et social. « Du côté des recettes, la pression fiscale franchira pour la première fois le seuil communautaire de 20%, pour s'établir à 21% dès 2027, grâce à une Stratégie de Recettes à Moyen Terme privilégiant l'élargissement de l'assiette, intégration du secteur informel, fiscalité foncière, taxation de l'économie numérique, sur le relèvement des taux », lit-on dans le texte. 4 326,3 milliards de dépenses courantes Il ressort aussi de ce document que les dépenses courantes, se situeraient à 4 326,3 milliards FCFA en 2029 contre 4 485,7 milliards FCFA en 2027. Pour les intérêts sur la dette publique, elles seraient payés à hauteur de 1 303,9 milliards FCFA en 2027 à 1 061,4 milliards FCFA en 2029. Il convient de noter aussi de noter que les charges sont projetées à 22 132,7 milliards FCFA et les prévisions de ressources sont attendues à 6 082,1 milliards FCFA. Quant aux dépenses, elles sont prévues à hauteur de 7 242,3 milliards FCFA. Ce qui laisse un déficit budgétaire 1 160,3 milliards FCFA. Concernant le Produit intérieur brut (PIB) nominal, il est évalué à 23 672,8 milliards FCFA. Les recettes du budget général sont projetées globalement sur la période triennale à 18 286,0 milliards FCFA constituées de recettes internes de 17 654,8 milliards FCFA et des recettes externes de 631,2 milliards FCFA. 5 527,0 milliards FCFA de recettes internes en 2027 Par rapport aux recettes internes, elles passent de 5 527,0 milliards FCFA en 2027 à 6 224,2 milliards FCFA en 2029. Les ressources externes, elles passeraient de 201,4 milliards FCFA à 220,2 milliards FCFA Pour les transferts courants y compris les subventions à différents secteurs passeraient de 1 220,3 milliards FCFA en 2027 à 1 195 milliards FCFA en 2029. Le document informe également que le besoin global de financement de l’économie estimé à 19 689,4 milliards FCFA et les Comptes Spéciaux du Trésor sont évalués à 941,9 milliards FCFA pendant cette période. Il urge aussi de souligner qu’en 2029, les recettes et dépenses des collectivités territoriales dotées de ressources propres avoisineront respectivement 389,3 milliards FCFA et 275,2 milliards FCFA. Mariama DIEME

items.title: Goods transporters to go on strike from Saturday after talks with govt fail
items.description: Goods transporters and oil tanker operators began suspending their services on Friday night after negotiations with the government failed, ahead of their nationwide wheel-jam strike scheduled for Saturday. All Pakistan Goods Transport Itehad spokesman and All Pakistan Goods Transport Owners Association President Mohammad Owais Chaudhry Advocate told Dawn that talks with Federal Minister for Communications Aleem Khan and other government officials had failed. He said the negotiations ended without a breakthrough, prompting transporters, including edible oil tanker operators, petroleum oil tanker operators, truckers, trailer operators and other intercity transporters, to proceed with their previously announced strike. “We have informed the government side about the problems we are facing and our concerns,” Chaudhry said, adding that the strike would continue until their demands were accepted. However, the minister has assured the transporters that he would discuss their demands, and the next round of talks would be held on Monday morning. The unified body of transporters had already announced that it would begin its wheel-jam strike from August 8, and warned that it would not be a token strike but an indefinite one. “Commercial goods carriers across the country have already been taken off the roads and will remain stationed at designated places during the protest period,” Chaudhry said. Among the key demands of the transporters is the uniform enforcement of axle-load limits across the country and permission for 10-wheel vehicles to carry up to 35 tonnes. They have also demanded reductions in diesel prices and toll taxes, besides seeking relief in withholding tax to ease the financial burden on the transport sector. The transporters have also called for the withdrawal of customs provisions that, according to the association, allow authorities to confiscate vehicles carrying goods found to be in violation of customs laws. Other demands include the withdrawal of the Punjab Highway Patrol’s powers to issue challans to commercial vehicles, an end to what the association described as unnecessary challans and excessive fines on motorways and highways, and measures to facilitate the issuance of heavy transport vehicle licences to drivers.

items.title: Sindh govt constitutes third medical board for exhumation of Mir Ali Raza’s body
items.description: After withdrawing its two earlier notifications, the Sindh government on Friday notified a newly constituted eight-member medical board to carry out the exhumation of 25-year-old business owner Mir Ali Raza’s body on Saturday. The exhumation, which was originally scheduled for Friday, was deferred after the deceased’s family objected to the abrupt reconstitution of the medical board, just hours after the notification of the first one. A notification issued by the Sindh Health Department on Friday named police surgeon Dr Sumaiyya Syed as the convener of the board and Dow University of Health Sciences (DUHS) Pathology Department head Professor Dr Naseem Ahmed as the pathologist. The eight-member board also includes Jinnah Sindh Medical University’s (JSMU) Dr Farah Waseem as a forensic expert, Shanakht Project’s Amir Hassan Khan as a forensic identification expert, Additional Police Surgeon Dr Srichand, Jinnah Post-Graduate Medical Centre (JPMC) medicolegal officers Dr Kamran Khan and Dr Daniyal Mirza, and Office of Police Surgeon Administrative In-charge Dr Muhammad. According to the notification, the board may also co-opt any expert member if required. Moreover, a notification issued by the Office of the Police Surgeon said that the exhumation of Ali’s body would be carried out on Saturday, August 8, at 11am. A civil judge and judicial magistrate Karachi-XXI would also be present, according to the police surgeon’s office. Reconstitution of board On Thursday, a Karachi court allowed the exhumation of Ali’s body on an application filed by the victim’s father, directing the police surgeon and the Sindh health secretary to constitute a medico-legal board for the exhumation of Ali’s body “at the earliest possible date and time”. The court ruling came after a controversy emerged between the Karachi police surgeon and investigators over alleged loopholes in the medico-legal report regarding the post-mortem examination. The Sindh Health Department then constituted the eight-member board, with the police surgeon as the convener. Dr Ahmed of Dow DUHS, Dr Waseem of JSMU, Amir Khan of Citizens Police Liaison Committee, Dr Sirichand, Dr Kamran and Dr Daniyal of JPCM and Dr Yaseen, the admin in-charge of the police surgeon’s office, were the other members of the board. However, a new order had been issued by the Sindh Health Directorate. The notification said that the board had been reconstituted to conduct the exhumation and medico-legal examination of the deceased. While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new board, its members were changed to Prof Dr Zakiuddin from DUHS, Prof Dr Kazi Akbar and Prof Dr Abid Hussain Chang from Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences and Hyderabad Police Surgeon Dr Waseem Khan. Controversy over autopsy Raza, owner of eatery Wafflix, had gone missing on July 28. The 25-year-old’s body was found a day later with a gunshot wound in bushes near Shahi Qila Ground in Gulistan-i-Jauhar. Initially, on the complaint lodged by his father, a case was registered at the Ferozabad police station under Section 365 (kidnapping or abducting with intent secretly and wrongfully to confine a person) of the Pakistan Penal Code. Police maintain that the investigation has revealed that Ali had been facing financial difficulties and had asked his friends for money the night he died. According to police, he had left his home in PECHS Block-2 and hired a taxi through an app. The taxi driver dropped him a short distance from the spot where his body was found, police said. The case took a new turn when Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed told a private news channel on Tuesday that the postmortem findings of Ali’s body had raised several questions, as some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs. She said the reported entry wound, bullet trajectory and exit wound did not correspond with one another. While it was scientifically possible for a bullet to enter through the back and exit from the front, she stressed that her assessment was based only on the postmortem report and photographs, as she had not examined the body herself. The police surgeon noted that entry wounds were typically smaller than exit wounds in firearm cases. She also said that gunshot residue, commonly found on the hands in suspected suicides, was not tested for in this case. Her interview prompted the police authorities to issue a statement, terming such observations as having the potential to adversely affect the ongoing investigation. The statement, however, said that exhumation of the dead body could be done on the medical board’s recommendation for further clarification by a committee of medico-legal experts with the court’s permission.

items.title: Vasty Arthur takes Tinsel Couture and Ghana’s Northern heritage to the global runway
items.description: Ghanaian fashion designer Vasty Arthur, Creative Director of Tinsel Couture, has taken the richness of Ghanaian culture to the international stage, presenting a striking collection inspired by Northern Ghana’s textile heritage at an international runway event in Kazan, Republic of Tatarstan, Russia. Through her collection, The Pride of the North, Vasty used fashion to tell a distinctly Ghanaian story rooted in craftsmanship, identity and the generations of artisans who have preserved the country’s traditional textile heritage. The collection was showcased at the 5th International Ethno-Fashion Festival “Lifestyle – Cultural Code,” an international gathering of designers, artisans, cultural leaders and fashion enthusiasts that celebrates fashion as an expression of living culture. For Vasty and Tinsel Couture, the event represented more than a fashion showcase. It was an opportunity to present Ghanaian design and craftsmanship to a global audience while demonstrating how traditional textiles can be transformed into contemporary fashion with international appeal From Northern Ghana to the World At the heart of The Pride of the North is one of Northern Ghana’s most recognisable cultural symbols—the traditional smock, popularly known as the fugu or batakari. Handwoven in narrow strips and carefully stitched together, the smock represents generations of craftsmanship, patience, resilience and community. Rather than reproducing traditional garments, Vasty Arthur reinterpreted the textile for the modern runway, combining its distinctive textures and cultural significance with contemporary silhouettes and refined tailoring. The result is a collection that remains unmistakably Ghanaian while demonstrating that indigenous textiles have a place in modern international fashion. This approach reflects the philosophy behind Tinsel Couture: preserving heritage while reimagining it for contemporary audiences. Under Vasty’s creative direction, traditional craftsmanship serves as a foundation for innovation, celebrating Ghana’s rich fashion heritage while exploring new possibilities. Fashion as Cultural Storytelling For Tinsel Couture, fashion is more than clothing—it is a medium for telling stories and celebrating identity. In The Pride of the North, the Northern smock is complemented by handwoven Kente and traditional tie-dye fabrics, bringing together some of Ghana’s most iconic textile traditions in a single contemporary collection. Kente, long associated with royalty, achievement, wisdom and identity, adds another layer of cultural symbolism, while the tie-dye fabrics highlight the creativity and individuality of Ghanaian artisans. Rather than allowing these textiles to compete, Vasty blends them into a cohesive visual narrative that reflects Ghana’s cultural diversity and shared national identity. The collection avoids turning traditional attire into costume. Instead, its modern silhouettes, thoughtful tailoring and wearable designs allow heritage to inspire fashion that speaks confidently to contemporary audiences. Designing with Purpose At the centre of this creative journey is Vasty Arthur, whose work continues to demonstrate the ability of Ghanaian designers to transform indigenous knowledge into fashion that resonates both locally and internationally. Her presentation in Kazan placed her alongside designers representing cultures from around the world. It also provided an opportunity to showcase Ghana through the skill of its artisans, the richness of its textiles and the creativity of its contemporary fashion industry. Each garment reflects the work of the people behind the fabric—from the weavers who preserve centuries-old techniques to the artisans whose craftsmanship remains central to Ghana’s cultural identity. By bringing their work to an international runway, Vasty Arthur and Tinsel Couture helped introduce these traditions to a wider global audience. Weaving Heritage into the Future An old Northern Ghanaian proverb says, “A single strand cannot weave a smock.” The saying speaks to collaboration, community and the many hands required to create something enduring. It also reflects the essence of The Pride of the North. Behind every garment is a chain of cultural knowledge—from those who spin and weave the threads to the artisans who preserve traditional techniques and the designer who reimagines them for a contemporary audience. Through Tinsel Couture, Vasty Arthur demonstrates that Ghanaian heritage need not be abandoned in pursuit of global relevance. Instead, it can serve as a source of creativity and innovation. Her appearance in Kazan was therefore more than a runway presentation. It celebrated Ghanaian creativity, honoured the artisans who continue to sustain the country’s textile traditions and reaffirmed the growing place of African fashion on the global stage. With The Pride of the North, Vasty Arthur and Tinsel Couture are not simply preserving Ghana’s textile heritage—they are reimagining it for a new generation and weaving it confidently into the future of global fashion.

items.title: 2027: Ortom debunks plot to replace Aondoakaa as Benue PDP guber candidate
items.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi Former Benue state governor and leader of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), in the state, Chief Samuel Ortom, has dismissed as false and misleading reports alleging that he and other party leaders are plotting to replace the party’s 2027 governorship candidate, Chief Michael Aondoakaa, SAN, with the Executive Secretary of the Nigerian Shippers’ Council, Dr. Pius Akutah. Ortom, in a statement issued by his Media Assistant, Zege Terhide, said the report circulating on social media was a “mischievous” distortion of a recent meeting involving prominent Benue stakeholders. The former governor explained that he, alongside the Senate Minority Leader, Senator Abba Moro, and the PDP governorship candidate, Aondoakaa, met with prominent Benue sons, including Chief Simon Shango, Prof. Iyorwuese Hagher, Dr. Pius Akutah, Emmanuel Ameh and Dr. Matthias Byuan. According to him, the meeting was part of ongoing consultations aimed at building a broad strategic alliance among Benue stakeholders for the overall interest of the state. “At no time during the meeting was the replacement of Chief Aondoakaa as the PDP governorship candidate discussed, contemplated or placed on the agenda,” Ortom said. He described attempts to give the meeting a different interpretation as mischievous, stressing that political consultations across party lines were normal in a democratic environment. “It is therefore mischievous for anyone to take a legitimate meeting of Benue leaders and manufacture an entirely different motive for it,” he said. Ortom maintained that consultations and engagements involving political actors and stakeholders should not automatically be interpreted as secret conspiracies, particularly when such engagements are motivated by the larger interest of the people. “Political consultations and engagements across party lines are neither strange nor secret conspiracies, particularly when they are driven by the larger interest of the people,” he stated. The former governor further put to rest speculation over the PDP governorship ticket, declaring unequivocally that Aondoakaa remains the party’s duly nominated candidate for the 2027 governorship election in the state. “Chief Michael Aondoakaa, SAN, remains the duly nominated governorship candidate of the PDP in Benue State for the 2027 election,” Ortom declared. He said the former Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice enjoys the confidence and support of the PDP leadership and members across the state. Ortom also expressed confidence in Aondoakaa’s ability to provide effective leadership if elected, citing his experience, competence and understanding of the challenges facing Benue. He said Aondoakaa had the capacity to reposition the state and provide purposeful leadership, particularly in the areas of security, economic recovery and sustainable development. The former governor therefore warned those responsible for circulating the alleged replacement story to desist from spreading what he described as fabricated narratives capable of causing confusion within the PDP and among supporters of its governorship candidate. “Political journalism and commentary must be anchored on facts, not conjecture, deliberate falsehood or the attribution of imaginary motives to legitimate engagements,” he cautioned. Ortom urged PDP members, supporters of Aondoakaa and the people of Benue State to disregard the report and remain focused on the party’s preparations for the 2027 elections. He stressed that the alleged misinformation would not distract the PDP leadership from its efforts to build what he described as a formidable coalition of Benue people capable of providing the state with a credible alternative in 2027. The post 2027: Ortom debunks plot to replace Aondoakaa as Benue PDP guber candidate appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: What is the Patriot missile system and why are supplies depleted worldwide?
items.description: First used in the 1991 Gulf War, the US Patriot air defence system has seen demand spike sharply this year, with supplies of interceptor missiles depleted by Ukraine’s war against the Russian invasion and the widening war in the Middle East. Ukraine is urgently seeking more Patriot interceptors to defend against a nightly barrage of Russian ballistic missile strikes. But the Iran war has drained arsenals in the US and the Gulf, and some European countries are holding onto missiles they may need for their own defence. The following are some details about the Patriot air defence system, one of the most advanced weapons in the US arsenal. What is the Patriot system? Patriot, short for Phased Array Tracking Radar for Intercept on Target, is a mobile surface-to-air missile defence system built by US weapons maker Raytheon Technologies that can be used in all kinds of weather and at long range. Developed in the 1980s, the Patriot system has been modernised over the past decades, expanding its capabilities and reach. It is slated to remain in service through 2048. A typical battery includes radar and control systems, a power unit, launchers, and support vehicles. The system can intercept aircraft, tactical ballistic missiles and cruise missiles, depending on the interceptor used. What can the Patriot system do? The system has different capabilities depending on the type of interceptor used. The earlier PAC-2 interceptor uses a blast-fragmentation warhead that detonates in the vicinity of a target, while the PAC-3 family of missiles uses more accurate “hit-to-kill” technology to physically collide with the target. Raytheon makes the PAC-2 GEM-T interceptor, which can defeat smaller, short-range ballistic missiles, cruise missiles or enemy aircraft. Lockheed Martin, the world’s largest arms maker, builds the more advanced PAC-3 Missile Segment Enhancement (MSE), which can hit longer-range ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, aircraft and also hypersonics. In July, Lockheed introduced a new interceptor, the PAC-3 Adapted Capability Effector (ACE), which it says will cost half as much while still being able to target short-range ballistic missiles, aircraft and cruise missiles. The system’s radar has a range of over 150 kilometres and can simultaneously track up to 100 potential targets, the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (Nato) said in 2015. Although not originally designed to intercept hypersonic weapons, in May 2023 the US confirmed Ukraine had used the Patriot system to shoot down a Russian Kinzhal missile, which Moscow claims is hypersonic. Countries closely guard details about the number of targets destroyed by Patriot systems, although Ukraine said in January it had destroyed 250 targets, including 140 ballistic missiles. Patriot has also destroyed dozens of Iranian ballistic missiles in the Gulf, although details have not been released. How widely is it used? Raytheon has built and delivered over 240 Patriot fire units, according to its website. Raytheon and Lockheed together have manufactured thousands of interceptor missiles. Nineteen countries now operate the Patriot system, according to Raytheon, including the US, Germany, Poland, Ukraine, Japan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Egypt. Of these countries, 16 have the newest PAC-3 MSE missiles, while six to eight countries have requested additional missiles to replenish their depleted stocks. In this US Army handout photo released on June 1, 2026, a US Army air defence artilleryman conducts maintenance on an MIM-104 Patriot missile system, the army’s primary terminal-phase anti-ballistic missile system, at an undisclosed location in the Middle East. — AFP/File How much does it cost? A newly produced single Patriot battery costs over $1 billion, including $400 million for the system and $690m for the missiles in a battery, according to the Centre for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS). Patriot PAC-3 interceptors are estimated at around $4m to $5m per missile. Why are supplies dwindling? Specific inventory numbers are classified, but CSIS estimates that about 65 per cent of US Patriot interceptors were expended between February and July, with less than 850 left on hand, down from 2,330 before the Iran war began. Current inventories in the Gulf states are also severely depleted, and several European countries have transferred some of their supplies to Ukraine , experts say. Saudi Arabia used about 86pc of its 2,800 PAC-3 interceptors in the first 38 days of combat, leaving it with 400 missiles left in April. Other Gulf nations used up similar amounts of their inventories, CSIS said. Are countries buying more Patriots to boost inventories? The US has approved the sale of 5,250 interceptors to Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates for replenishment. The US is also pressing ahead with talks on allowing Ukraine to make Patriot interceptor missiles, even after President Donald Trump cast doubt on such a deal, sources familiar with the discussions said. The talks include an option for Ukraine to build some components for final assembly elsewhere in Europe. Last month, the US Army awarded Lockheed Martin a contract worth up to $58.6bn to produce Patriot interceptor missiles.

items.title: Is the “Democracy Under Attack” narrative real, or is it a convenient escape from accountability?
items.description: The opposition has marched in red and black, chanting that democracy is under attack. The slogans are loud, the placards are colourful, and the cameras are rolling. But beneath the spectacle lies a simple question: What exactly is under attack? Is democracy under attack because former public officials are being investigated over decisions they took while exercising public power? If accountability has suddenly become oppression, then every anti-corruption institution should probably close shop. Is democracy under attack because people who allegedly spread falsehoods or make threatening statements are invited to answer before the law? Freedom of expression has never included a licence to publish anything without consequence. Rights exist alongside responsibilities. Or is democracy under attack because political actors who once wielded the full machinery of the state now find themselves on the receiving end of the same legal processes they once defended? There is a certain irony in watching those who once insisted that “the law must take its course” suddenly discover the vocabulary of victimhood when the law knocks on their own doors. This is not to suggest that any government is above criticism. Every administration must be scrutinised, and every abuse of power must be resisted. Democracy thrives on dissent. But democracy also thrives on consistency. If accountability was patriotic yesterday, it cannot become persecution simply because the names on the docket have changed. The greatest weakness of the “Democracy Under Attack” narrative is that it asks Ghanaians to suffer from selective amnesia. Citizens remember the years when journalists complained of intimidation, when critics accused the state of heavy-handedness, and when public confidence in governance steadily declined. Those memories cannot simply be erased with matching T-shirts and dramatic slogans. Even more striking is the leadership presenting itself as the guardian of democratic values. A party once admired for discipline, intellectual depth, and organisational strength increasingly appears trapped between defending its past and explaining its present. Rather than offering a compelling alternative vision, it seems preoccupied with portraying accountability as oppression. Of course, every political party has the constitutional right to demonstrate. Peaceful protest is itself an expression of democratic freedom. Ironically, the very ability to organise nationwide demonstrations, criticise the government publicly, and march through the streets under police protection is evidence that democratic space continues to exist. Perhaps the demonstration was less about saving democracy and more about energising a discouraged political base. There is nothing inherently wrong with mobilising supporters. Political parties do it everywhere. But dressing ordinary political mobilisation in the robes of a constitutional emergency risks diminishing genuine threats to democracy when they actually arise. Democracy is not endangered because former officeholders are called upon to account for their stewardship. We need a vigilant and constructive opposition not those full of hypocrisy. We deserve robust criticism of government and principled defenders of constitutionalism in honesty. If every investigation becomes “persecution,” every prosecution becomes “dictatorship,” and every legal process becomes “an attack on democracy,” then the phrase itself loses all meaning. Sometimes the loudest cries of “Save Democracy” are really pleas to save politicians from accountability.

items.title: Car dealer shot dead, wife critically injured in attack at Tuba Beach Drive Estate
items.description: A 50-year-old car dealer has been shot dead, while his wife is in critical condition after unidentified gunmen attacked the couple outside their home at Beach Drive Estate near Tuba in the Ga South Municipality of the Greater Accra Region. The deceased, Kwesi Rahman, was reportedly returning home with his wife from an evening walk when the incident occurred at about 9:30 p.m. on Thursday, August 6. According to eyewitnesses, the couple had just arrived at the entrance to their residence when an unidentified assailant emerged and opened fire on them. Mr. Rahman sustained multiple gunshot wounds and died instantly at the scene, while his wife was also shot several times. Residents who heard the gunfire rushed to the scene and assisted in transporting the injured woman to a nearby hospital, where she is receiving treatment. For security and medical reasons, the facility where she is being treated has not been disclosed. Speaking to Adom News, an eyewitness, Faustina Antwi, said the body of the deceased had been conveyed to the police morgue for preservation and autopsy. A resident who witnessed the aftermath of the attack said the sound of gunfire sent residents rushing from their homes. “I was outside around 9:50 when I heard what sounded like a gunshot. So I quickly went inside and told my mum that I had heard gunshots. When we came out, we saw people coming from down there. When I got there, I saw him lying in front of his gate. I didn’t see anybody and I didn’t hear any noise. It was just the gunshot I heard,” the resident recounted. The incident has left residents of Beach Drive Estate shaken, with many expressing concern over security in the community. Some residents have called on the Ghana Police Service to intensify security patrols within the estate to protect lives and property and restore confidence among residents. A relative of the deceased also appealed to the police to conduct a thorough investigation to identify those responsible and bring them to justice. Police have since launched investigations into the shooting and are working to identify and arrest the gunman behind the attack. Mr. Rahman, who celebrated his 50th birthday in July this year, was well known in the community as a car dealer. Authorities are yet to establish the motive behind the attack.

items.title: Bobo-Dioulasso : Une nouvelle centrale thermique de 26,4 MW renforce les capacités de production d’électricité
items.description: Le Burkina Faso poursuit le renforcement de son autonomie énergétique. Le ministre de l'Énergie, des Mines et des Carrières, Yacouba Zabré Gouba, a officiellement mis en service, ce 7 août 2026 à Bobo-Dioulasso, la nouvelle centrale thermique de Bobo II d'une capacité de 26,4 MW. Réalisée en 15 mois pour un investissement de plus de 33 milliards de FCFA, cette infrastructure énergétique permet de porter la capacité totale de la centrale de Bobo II de 60 MW à 86,4 MW et marque une nouvelle étape dans la politique gouvernementale de consolidation de l'offre nationale d'électricité. Elle permet également au Burkina Faso de franchir une nouvelle étape dans sa stratégie de renforcement de la production nationale d'électricité. La nouvelle centrale est équipée de trois groupes électrogènes de dernière génération développant chacun une puissance de 8,8 MW Selon le directeur général de la SONABEL, Souleymane Ouédraogo, la nouvelle centrale est équipée de trois groupes électrogènes de dernière génération développant chacun une puissance de 8,8 MW, soit une capacité totale installée de 26,4 MW. L'installation fonctionne principalement au fuel lourd, tandis que le diesel est utilisé pour le démarrage des moteurs et comme combustible de secours. Pour le ministre Yacouba Zabré Gouba, cette réalisation répond à une ambition claire qui celle d’accroître les capacités nationales de production, réduire progressivement la dépendance du Burkina Faso aux importations d'énergie et garantir un approvisionnement plus stable aux populations et aux entreprises. Pour lui, la centrale constitue alors un investissement stratégique pour le pays. Elle permettra de renforcer durablement le système électrique tout en accompagnant le développement économique et industriel. Le projet a été réalisé en 15 mois au lieu de 24 mois comme prévu L'électricité produite par cette infrastructure sera injectée dans le Réseau national interconnecté (RNI), permettant ainsi d'améliorer la qualité et la disponibilité de l'énergie électrique sur l'ensemble du territoire. Le ministre a également salué la performance des équipes techniques ayant conduit le projet. Alors que les travaux étaient programmés pour une durée de 24 mois, la centrale a été réalisée en seulement 15 mois, soit neuf mois avant l'échéance initiale. Une prouesse qui permettra d'accroître plus rapidement les capacités nationales de production dans un contexte où la demande en électricité ne cesse de croître. La centrale de Bobo II traduit la volonté des autorités burkinabè d'investir dans des infrastructures structurantes Cette nouvelle centrale s'inscrit dans le vaste programme gouvernemental de développement des infrastructures énergétiques, engagé afin de renforcer la souveraineté énergétique du Burkina Faso. Après la mise en service de la centrale thermique de Pabré le 21 juillet dernier, le gouvernement entend poursuivre cette dynamique avec l'entrée en exploitation prochaine des centrales thermiques de Koudougou et de Kaya, d'une capacité de 25 MW chacune. Ces nouvelles infrastructures viendront renforcer davantage le parc national de production et contribuer à sécuriser l'alimentation électrique du pays. Au-delà des chiffres, la mise en service de la centrale de Bobo II traduit la volonté des autorités burkinabè d'investir dans des infrastructures structurantes capables de soutenir la croissance économique, d'améliorer la compétitivité des entreprises et d'offrir aux populations un meilleur accès à une électricité fiable. items.title: US appeals court halts Trump ballroom project paving way for Supreme Court showdown
items.description: The Trump administration has been ordered to stop construction on President Donald Trump’s $400m (£297m) ballroom at the White House. A federal appeals court dealt the latest setback to the controversial project on Friday, testing Trump’s presidential authority and paving the way for a Supreme Court showdown on appeal. “Whether or not a ⁠massive ballroom should be constructed is for Congress to decide and is not a matter for Executive self-help,” the panel’s ​majority said. The order upholds a preliminary ​injunction won by the National Trust for Historic Preservation, which sued after the administration tore down the ​East Wing last year to begin the project without congressional approval. “Congress has not ceded unfettered authority to the Executive Branch to dramatically redesign, reshape, and reconstruct the White House — the People’s ​House — to fit a particular President’s desires,” the panel said. The three-judge panel, in a 2-1 decision, said: “Each President is a temporary tenant, not the owner, of the White House and its Executive Residence.” “The President has no — and claims no — constitutionally assigned authority over that property, which is designed and maintained for the use of all Presidents, current and future, and for the American people,” the opinion said. The administration appealed to the court after a federal judge twice blocked above-ground construction on the ballroom, while still allowing underground work to proceed. The ruling on Friday upholds that order blocking above-ground construction without congressional approval. The appeals court delayed implementation of its ruling for 14 days to allow the Trump administration to appeal to the Supreme Court. The BBC has contacted the White House and Department of Justice for comment. Construction at the site where the East Wing previously stood was previously ordered to stop, but a court delayed the ruling allowing construction to continue while the appeals court considered briefs and heard arguments last month, according to the BBC’s US media partner CBS. President Trump has asserted that the new ballroom is needed to “accommodate people for grand parties, State Visits”, and has also said that it is “vital for National Security”. He doubled down on the need for the space after an assassination attempt at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner in April. The three-judge panel on Friday said that its ruling “has nothing at all to do with whether the proposed ballroom is desirable”, nor does it weigh in on whether the administration may ultimately construct the ballroom. “What it does mean is that the Defendants may not do so during the district court’s expeditious litigation without securing Congress’s authorization, as the Constitution and laws require,” the order said. The National Trust for Historic Preservation celebrated the latest ruling, noting that no above-ground construction can take place “unless and until” Congress takes action. “The White House, a global landmark that symbolizes American identity and the ideals of democracy, belongs to the American people,” said Brent Leggs, President and CEO of the National Trust. “The National Trust for Historic Preservation and its partners are proud to defend this irreplaceable monument on behalf of all Americans.”

Il a egalement indique un dynamisme de l'economie nationale, assurant que la Cote d'Ivoire disposait d'un taux de croissance annuel des « plus eleves de la region et du monde, confirmant la solidite de ses fondamentaux ». Il s'est engage dans ce contexte a poursuivre les efforts pour renforcer les acces a l'eau potable, a l'electricite, aux soins de sante, a une education de qualite, au logement et a des services publics toujours plus performants. Il a aussi souligne l'engagement de son gouvernement pour ameliorer la situation de l'emploi, du pouvoir d'achat et pour proteger les plus vulnerables. À vous, #femmes et #hommes qui travaillez la #terre ivoirienne : merci. Ce vendredi, à #Yopougon , notre pays a célébré ses 66 ans d'indépendance aux côtés du Président @AOuattara_PRCI . Parmi les temps forts : un hommage à l' #agriculture ivoirienne, à travers de beaux tableaux… pic.twitter.com/oV2tCxJ58B — Bruno Nabagné KONÉ (@Bruno_N_Kone) August 7, 2026 Grâce presidentielle pour 4 661 detenus de droit commun Alassane Ouattara a signe deux decrets au titre de la Justice. Un premier accordant la grâce presidentielle a 2 064 detenus, alors que le second stipule une remise de peine a 2 597 detenus dont le reliquat de la peine est inferieur a trente-six mois. Les deux textes combines accordent donc la liberte a 4 661 detenus de droit commun, condamnes pour des infractions mineures.

items.title: The Internet Is in Crisis
items.description: Almost 20 years ago, I had tickets to see Amy Winehouse perform in London, at a show that was canceled just an hour before it was scheduled to start. A friend and I went to a nearby hotel bar instead, and not much later, in walked Winehouse herself—tiny, grubby, and completely incoherent. She walked over to us and stared, her eyes both furious and vacant, until someone in her entourage came and dragged her away. I remember the person who flashed to mind in that bizarre moment: the gossip blogger Perez Hilton. If you weren’t regularly online during the late 2000s, it’s hard to explain how dominant a presence Hilton was—how incessantly he posted about what celebrities might be doing on any given day, how shameless he was about posting upskirt photos, how judgmental his tirades about young women in crisis were. His fiendish MO was lifting pictures from paparazzi agencies and then scribbling penises or obscene epithets on them in order to claim fair use. Hilton—whose real name is Mario Lavandeira Jr.—was particularly cruel about Winehouse, who was being photographed by the celebrity press almost daily in states of disarray. He posted, by turns, about her physical appearance (“super skinny, dirty and wasted”), false rumors of her pregnancy (“We were sure that her ovaries were too gin-soaked to be of any use”), and a performance in which she wasn’t wearing underwear (“Grrrossss!!!!!!!!! Who needs to see cracked out snatch?”). PerezHilton.com was relentless and brutal, and its readers could not get enough, especially when the blog’s coverage collided with moments of calamitous celebrity breakdown. (When the actor Lindsay Lohan was arrested in 2007, the site reportedly received 8.8 million pageviews that day.) Since then, the internet has metastasized into something officially kinder—we no longer berate famous people in crisis for sport quite as much as we used to—and quietly more appalling, where irony-poisoned young men broadcast their executions and social-media companies seem to basically shrug in response. And so, on Tuesday night, during what seemed to be a mental-health breakdown of his own, Hilton was able to stream himself live on TikTok cutting himself with a knife for about 15 minutes before his broadcast was finally interrupted. Any number of Hilton’s followers on TikTok could have clicked on the stream thinking they were going to see a standard broadcast about Ariana Grande or Trader Joe’s ready meals (both of which Hilton had posted about on YouTube in recent weeks). Instead, they got a scene of unimaginable violence. “I am fine with horror/gore, have seen a lot real and fake, and this was so deeply disturbing I could not get the image out of my head all night,” one commenter posted on Reddit . Another added, “I watch cartel torture and beheading videos with no issues. I had to turn the perez video off after about 20 seconds, and I felt deeply disturbed for hours.” TikTok’s failure to interrupt Hilton’s broadcast for such a long time, even as horrified viewers were reporting it, is astonishing. (A spokesperson for the site told Wired that a “moderator error” caused a delay in removal; another told Vanity Fair that Hilton was persistent in his attempts to broadcast what he was doing, using several different streams to do so.) [ Read: The unspeakable, enabled ] In the United States, Section 230 of the Communications Act shields technology and communication companies from being held legally responsible for third-party content that appears on their platforms. And since Facebook launched livestreaming in 2015, social-media sites have struggled to establish safeguards for atrocities being broadcast in real time, to the point where the phenomenon of people livestreaming their own attempts to die has become “ an emerging public health crisis ,” in the words of psychology researchers. After a man livestreamed himself killing 51 people at two mosques in New Zealand in 2019 on Facebook Live, Facebook said it was investing in “technical innovation” to prevent people from abusing its platform. Nevertheless, footage of mass shootings and other atrocities proliferates globally before befuddled tech companies can tie their shoes. The tone of the contemporary internet is also darker and more nihilist than it has ever been. “Social-media platforms—and especially X—have loosened their grip on moderation at the same time that AI tools have allowed for the easy proliferation of slop,” my colleague Charlie Warzel wrote earlier this year. “Never before has there been so much cynical, cruel content and trolling.” But the idea that Hilton might end up turning self-harm into content feels particularly fraught. A statement from his family posted online said that the influencer had been “experiencing a severe mental-health crisis,” and that his three children, his niece, and his sister were at home with Hilton when he began hurting himself, although they left immediately “to protect the children from witnessing any further trauma.” Over the past decade and a half, Hilton has tried to pivot away from the bilious celebrity coverage that made him so successful: In a 2010 video, he announced that he would no longer be cruel. But his popularity never quite recovered, and he argued in his 2020 memoir, TMI , that the toxicity of his site was what had appealed to his readers, even if they didn’t want to admit it to themselves: “The more snarky names I gave the celebrities, the more penises or coke or boogers I drew on pictures of them, the more people visited my page.” It’s also true that PerezHilton.com peaked in its cultural relevance around 2007, the year that celebrity after celebrity seemed to be breaking down in public while pursued by paparazzi on mopeds. That year, Britney Spears shaved her head (when the actor Heath Ledger died in 2008, Hilton sold T-shirts emblazoned with the words Why Couldn’t It Be Britney? ), Anna-Nicole Smith overdosed on prescription medication, Lohan was arrested for cocaine possession, Paris Hilton went to jail, and Mischa Barton was arrested for driving under the influence of alcohol. Hilton documented each of these moments in vivid and elaborate detail—my browser finally quit when I got to page 79 of his archives related to Amy Winehouse—because he understood what people wanted from him and his work. “When Britney Spears was at her wildest, people were glued to my website,” he wrote in TMI. It’s impossible to know whether this awareness informed what he did to himself this week, and how he did it. Hilton’s breakdown is desperately sad; I’m haunted by the idea of what his children might have seen happen in their home, but also by the idea of what all children might see, at any time, in this hopelessly corrupted and seemingly unsalvageable internet. If you are having thoughts of suicide, please know that you are not alone. If you are in danger of acting on suicidal thoughts, call 911. For support and resources, call the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 988 or text 741-741 for the Crisis Text Line.

items.title: The Case for Calling People on the Phone
items.description: This is an edition of The Wonder Reader, a newsletter in which our editors recommend a set of stories to spark your curiosity and fill you with delight. Sign up here to get it every Saturday morning. Conversation has become optimized—but not always for the better. We send a quick text instead of making a call, react with an emoji instead of a laugh, and turn catching up into a series of efficient updates. Although staying in touch with people is easier than ever, we spend surprisingly little time talking to one another. “No one picks up the phone anymore,” Alexis C. Madrigal wrote in 2018. That’s in part because too many faceless telemarketers have our number, and in part because more people have come to treat phone calls as something to reserve for emergencies or bad news or major life events. However, in many cases they’re the easiest way to have conversations that texting can’t quite convey—ones that meander, surprise you, and leave you feeling a little more connected than before. Texting has made communication faster and more efficient, but not necessarily more conversational. Today’s newsletter is a reminder that you don’t need a reason or an agenda to call someone you’ve been thinking about. On Conversation Talk to People on the Telephone By Amanda Mull It’s time to start calling your friends again. ( From 2019 ) Read the article. Why No One Answers Their Phone Anymore By Alexis C. Madrigal Telephone culture is disappearing. ( From 2018 ) Read the article. Another Symptom of Growing Isolation By Olga Khazan A recent study found that people spoke fewer words a day in 2019 than in 2005. Read the article. Still Curious? The tension that defines modern life : Most people have a smartphone. But many want to use it less, Julie Beck writes. Maybe don’t send that voice note . The audio messages can encourage selfishness—unless you use them gracefully, Jacob Sweet argued in 2024. Other Diversions Bring back the blue-book exam. The dishonesty of true crime The new parent trap PS Courtesy of Bonnie B. My colleague Isabel Fattal recently asked readers to share a photo of something that sparks their sense of awe in the world. “My sense of awe for this world comes from my backyard, where a family of barred owls nests each year and produces angelic chicks that begin their lives playing among the trees,” Bonnie B. from Cordova, Tennessee, shared. “They make me believe in the magic of life.” We’ll continue to feature your responses in the coming weeks. — Rafaela

items.title: Maison d’Arrêt et de Correction (MAC) de Hann: trente détenus mineurs formés à la plomberie
items.description: L'Administration pénitentiaire poursuit sa politique de réinsertion sociale et professionnelle des personnes privées de liberté. Trente détenus mineurs de la Maison d'Arrêt et de Correction (MAC) de Hann bénéficient actuellement d'une formation professionnelle en plomberie, financée par le Fonds de Financement de la Formation Professionnelle et Technique (3FPT). D'une durée de trois mois, le programme combine apprentissages théoriques et pratiques : installation, entretien et réparation des équipements et réseaux sanitaires. À l'issue de la formation, les bénéficiaires disposeront d'une qualification directement mobilisable sur le marché du travail un secteur où la demande de main-d'œuvre qualifiée reste forte au Sénégal. Un pari sur l'avenir des jeunes détenus Au-delà du geste technique, c'est une logique de réinsertion durable que l'Administration pénitentiaire entend consolider. En misant sur la formation plutôt que sur la seule sanction, l'institution cherche à offrir à ces jeunes détenus des outils concrets d'autonomie, susceptibles de faciliter leur retour à la vie active une fois leur peine purgée. Cette démarche s'inscrit dans une approche plus large de prévention de la récidive, où l'investissement dans les compétences devient un levier d'inclusion socio-économique. Pour l'Administration pénitentiaire, chaque parcours de formation réussi représente un pas de plus vers une sortie de détention mieux préparée et une chance supplémentaire donnée à ces mineurs de se reconstruire. C.G.D

Burkina Faso : Farakan Labs lance PengMe, une plateforme pour faciliter l’avance sur salaire en cas d’urgence
items.description: La startup studio burkinabè Farakan Labs a officiellement lancé, ce 7 août 2026 à Ouagadougou, PengMe (« Prête-moi » en mooré), une plateforme numérique destinée à rapprocher les particuliers et les entreprises de solutions de financement d'urgence. Premier service proposé : une avance sur salaire digitalisée, accessible via une application mobile. Face aux difficultés que rencontrent de nombreux travailleurs pour accéder rapidement à des liquidités en cas d'imprévu, Farakan Labs propose une réponse numérique avec PengMe . Disponible sur les plateformes de téléchargement d'applications mobiles, cette solution ambitionne de simplifier les démarches d'avance sur salaire, notamment pour les salariés non bancarisés qui perçoivent néanmoins des revenus réguliers. Pour illustrer l'intérêt de cette innovation, Jérôme Kaboré, cofondateur de Farakan Labs, évoque le cas d'un salarié payé en espèces dont l'enfant tombe malade en soirée, alors qu'aucun responsable des ressources humaines n'est disponible pour traiter une demande d'avance sur salaire. « L'urgence financière ne prévient pas », résume-t-il. Selon lui, un salarié disposant d'un revenu régulier ne devrait pas être contraint de solliciter ses proches pour faire face à une dépense urgente. Le fonctionnement de PengMe place les entreprises au cœur du dispositif. Celles-ci souscrivent à la plateforme et déterminent les règles d'utilisation : ouverture des périodes d'avance sur salaire, fixation des plafonds, validation des employés éligibles et supervision du processus. Les salariés concernés créent ensuite leur compte personnel, relié à celui de leur entreprise. Après les vérifications d'identité, ils peuvent soumettre leurs demandes directement depuis l'application, dans les limites définies par leur employeur. Une fois la demande validée par les partenaires financiers de PengMe, les fonds sont transférés électroniquement. Le remboursement est ensuite effectué par l’employeur au moment du paiement des salaires. « À la fin du mois, on sait que c'est le responsable de la paie qui verse les salaires. Comme lui a accès à la plateforme, une facture lui est envoyée et c'est lui qui fait le virement sur le compte qu'on aura assigné », explique Jérôme Kaboré. Lors de la démonstration technique, le cofondateur et directeur technique de Farakan Labs, Irmeya Ouédraogo, a précisé que le plafond actuel est fixé à 50 000 FCFA , avec une limite correspondant au quart du salaire du bénéficiaire. Ces paramètres pourront évoluer au fur et à mesure du développement de la plateforme. « Nous ne sommes pas une institution financière. Nous sommes en discussion avec les institutions financières qui vont porter, derrière, cette initiative. Nous sommes l'interface que l'utilisateur utilise pour communiquer avec ces institutions », a-t-il souligné. Pour cette phase de lancement, l'utilisation de PengMe est gratuite pour les entreprises qui souhaitent adhérer au service. À terme, Farakan Labs prévoit d'élargir l'offre de PengMe à d'autres solutions de financement d'urgence destinées aux particuliers, aux micro-entreprises et aux PME. Les promoteurs envisagent notamment des produits liés au financement du fonds de roulement, des bons de commande, de l'affacturage ou encore des services d'assurance, en partenariat avec des institutions financières agréées. Pour Jérôme Kaboré, le projet est né du constat que de nombreux salariés, commerçants, micro-entrepreneurs et dirigeants de PME disposent d'activités rentables, mais peinent à obtenir rapidement des ressources financières lorsqu'un besoin urgent survient, notamment en dehors des horaires d'ouverture des banques. Avec PengMe, Farakan Labs entend ainsi accélérer la digitalisation des services financiers d'urgence au Burkina Faso. En jouant le rôle d'interface entre les utilisateurs, les entreprises et les institutions financières, la startup ambitionne de rendre l'accès à des financements rapides plus simple, plus sécurisé et mieux adapté aux réalités du quotidien des travailleurs et des entrepreneurs. Josué TIENDREBEOGO Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : Farakan Labs lance PengMe, une plateforme pour faciliter l'avance sur salaire en cas d'urgence est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Afrique de l’Ouest: la BIDC engage plus de 510 millions de Dollars US pour accélérer le développement
items.description: Le Conseil d'Administration de la Banque d'Investissement et de Développement de la CEDEAO (BIDC) a approuvé cinq opérations stratégiques d'un montant total de plus de 269,55 millions d'euros et 200 millions de dollars US, soit plus de 510 millions de dollars US d'engagements financiers. Ces opérations soutiendront des investissements dans les infrastructures de transport, la santé, les énergies renouvelables et le développement du secteur privé en Afrique de l'Ouest. Les décisions ont été prises lors de la 100ème réunion du Conseil d'Administration de la Banque, présidée par Dr George Agyekum Donkor, Président de la BIDC et de son Conseil d'administration. Elles témoignent de l'engagement constant de l'institution à financer des investissements à fort impact, favorisant la croissance économique et générant des résultats durables de développement dans la région. Les principales opérations approuvées : • Guinée – Infrastructures routières : 143,06 millions d'euros pour la construction et le revêtement de 84 kilomètres de routes sur les axes Cissela-Banko-N'Dèma et Banko-Saraya. Ce projet contribuera à l'amélioration des corridors de transport, à la facilitation des échanges commerciaux et à la réduction des coûts de transport. • Guinée – Santé : 65,87 millions d'euros pour la construction d'un hôpital régional de 200 lits à Siguiri. Cette infrastructure permettra d'élargir l'accès aux soins de santé spécialisés à plus de 1,7 million de personnes. • Guinée – Énergies renouvelables : 60,62 millions d'euros pour le financement du projet hydroélectrique de Tinkisso II, doté d'une capacité installée de 11 mégawatts et d'une production annuelle estimée à 48 gigawattheures. Le projet fournira une électricité propre à plus de 350 000 personnes. • Ghana – Infrastructures de transport : 150 millions de dollars US sous forme de ligne de crédit en faveur de Maripoma Enterprise Limited afin de soutenir huit projets stratégiques de routes et de ponts dont le portefeuille global est estimé à environ 1,2 milliard de dollars US. L'opération vise à renforcer la connectivité et à stimuler l'activité économique. • Sierra Léone – Secteur financier : 50 millions de dollars US sous forme de prêt subordonné accordé à WAICA Reinsurance Corporation Plc. Ce financement permettra de renforcer les fonds propres de l'entreprise et d'accroître sa capacité de financement dans les secteurs des infrastructures, de l'énergie, des transports et de l'agriculture, tout en favorisant l'intégration des normes environnementales, sociales et de gouvernance (ESG). Commentant les décisions du Conseil, Dr George Agyekum Donkor a souligné que ces opérations soutiennent des investissements transformateurs visant à renforcer l'intégration régionale, à élargir l'accès aux services essentiels, à promouvoir l'énergie durable et à mobiliser davantage de ressources au profit du développement du secteur privé. Il a indiqué que ces initiatives s'inscrivent pleinement dans le mandat de la BIDC et reflètent l'engagement de la Banque à améliorer durablement les conditions de vie des populations ouest-africaines. Ces financements approuvés, contribuent également à la mise en œuvre de la Stratégie GRO (Croissance, Résilience et Optimisation) 2026-2030 de la BIDC, qui vise à accélérer la transformation structurelle de l'Afrique de l'Ouest grâce à des investissements catalytiques. En soutenant des projets capables de libérer le potentiel productif, de stimuler l'investissement privé et de renforcer la compétitivité économique, la Banque contribue à jeter les bases d'une plus grande autonomie économique, d'une prospérité durable et d'une amélioration du niveau de vie des populations de la sous-région. *********************************** À propos de la BIDC La Banque d'Investissement et de Développement de la CEDEAO (BIDC) est l'Institution de Financement du Développement des quinze États de l’Afrique de l’Ouest. Basée à Lomé, en République togolaise, la Banque s'engage à financer des projets et programmes de développement portant sur diverses initiatives dans les secteurs des infrastructures et des services sociaux de base, du développement rural et de l'environnement, de l'industrie ainsi que des services sociaux, à travers ses guichets dédiés aux secteurs privé et public. Les interventions de la BIDC se font sous forme de prêts à long, moyen et court terme, de prises de participation, d’octroi de lignes de crédit et mise en place d’accords-cadres de refinancement, des opérations d'ingénierie financière et services connexes. www.bidc-ebid.org Contact Presse Unité de Communication et Relations Extérieures asomda@bidc-ebid.org +228 22 21 68 64 L’article Afrique de l'Ouest: la BIDC engage plus de 510 millions de Dollars US pour accélérer le développement est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Kozah/Changements climatiques : Des professionnels des médias en atelier de vulgarisation des PRA
items.description: Kara, 7 août (ATOP) – Des professionnels des médias publics et privés participent, du 6 au 8 août à Kara, à un atelier de vulgarisation des Plans régionaux d’adaptation (PRA) et de renforcement des compétences en matière de changement climatique. La rencontre, organisée par l’Association togolaise des journalistes engagés pour l’environnement (ATJ2E), est financé par l’Organisation des Nations Unies pour l’alimentation et l’agriculture (FAO). Elle intervient dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du projet NAP Readiness, « Renforcement des capacités nationales et régionales pour une gestion efficace des risques climatiques au Togo ». L’objectif est de renforcer les connaissances des journalistes venus de toutes les régions, sur les enjeux des changements climatiques. Il s’agit de les amener à contribuer à la vulgarisation des PRA à travers des productions de contenus impactant, fondés sur des données fiables et adaptées aux réalités de leurs communautés respectives. Le président de l’ATJ2E lors de sa présentation Les participants seront édifiés sur des modules, à savoir : les notions fondamentales en lien avec les changements climatiques et leurs impacts ; le cadre institutionnel national et international, et les PRA. Ils prendront également connaissance des projets et programmes de Restauration des paysages forestiers (RPF) au Togo. Les journalistes vont, en outre, expérimenter leur rôle et responsabilité face à l’urgence climatique par la découverte des réalités du terrain dans trois localités : la Kozah, la Binah et le Doufelgou. Le directeur de la Radio Kara, Takou John a, au nom de la ministre de la Communication, salué l’initiative qui vient situer davantage les journalistes sur leur rôle dans la lutte contre les changements climatiques. Il les a exhortés à faire des productions en langues locales afin de mieux éclairer les populations sur l’ampleur du phénomène et les mesures d’adaptation mises en place par le gouvernement en vue d’une meilleure résilience. Le coordonnateur du projet NAP Readiness, FAO, Dr. Pereki Hodabalo a relevé l’importance des questions relatives au climat, à la RPF et à l’adaptation, demandant que les informations liées soient traitées avec rigueur. « Vous êtes des relais d’information, des éducateurs, des acteurs de changement et des partenaires essentiels du développement durable. Grâce à vos reportages, vos émissions, vos chroniques et vos contenus numériques, vous rendez accessibles les informations parfois complexes, dans le cadre de la valorisation des bonnes pratiques et de la promotion des initiatives innovantes », a-t-il souligné. Le président de l’ATJ2E, Hector Sanndo Nammangue a invité ses confrères à être de véritables partenaires de développement, capables d’expliquer les politiques publiques, de valoriser les solutions locales et de rapprocher les connaissances scientifiques des communautés à la base. Il a convié les journalistes à produire des contenus beaucoup plus pertinents sur les enjeux climatiques. ​ATOP/TAL/BA/DHK

items.title: Burkina Faso : Le ministère de la Santé lance E-agrement, sa plateforme de gestion des procédures
items.description: Le ministère de la Santé a procédé, ce 7 août 2026 à Ouagadougou, au lancement officiel de « E-Agrement » , une plateforme numérique dédiée à la gestion dématérialisée des agréments. Cet outil vise à simplifier les procédures administratives liées aux demandes de conventions de partenariat avec le ministère ainsi qu’aux autorisations d’ouverture et d’exploitation des établissements privés de santé. Accessible sur internet, la plateforme permet aux usagers d’effectuer leurs démarches sans avoir à se déplacer. Après la création d’un compte, ils peuvent soumettre en ligne une demande de convention de partenariat ou une demande d’autorisation d’ouverture et d’exploitation d’un établissement privé de santé. Selon Jean-Serge Ouattara, directeur des systèmes d’information du ministère de la Santé, la plateforme guide l’usager tout au long de la procédure. Une fois la démarche sélectionnée, la liste des pièces constitutives du dossier est affichée. L’usager téléverse ensuite les documents requis, renseigne un formulaire et soumet son dossier à l’administration. Après le dépôt, les services compétents procèdent à l’analyse du dossier. Si des informations complémentaires sont nécessaires, le demandeur est invité à les fournir via la plateforme. À défaut, l’autorisation peut être accordée. « Le fait qu'on puisse accéder directement en ligne va permettre de réduire les déplacements et les coûts. Sur cette plateforme, c'est transparent pour l'usager puisqu'il soumet son dossier, tous les services habilités l'analysent et font leurs recommandations. Il peut suivre son dossier en temps réel sans se déplacer. On peut avoir la traçabilité de tout ce qui a été fait sur son dossier et cela raccourcit aussi les délais de traitement pour les services du ministère », a expliqué Jean-Serge Ouattara. Opérationnelle depuis la fin du mois d’avril 2026, la plateforme n’a été officiellement lancée qu’après l’obtention de l’autorisation du ministère chargé de la Transition digitale. Jean-Serge Ouattara a également précisé que la commission de la Coordination des programmes et projets du ministère, qui se réunit tous les deux mois, examine les dossiers soumis. Lorsque ceux-ci sont conformes aux exigences, les agréments sont délivrés. L'interface de la plateforme E-Agrement Pour le ministre de la Santé, Lucien Kargougou, cette innovation traduit la volonté de son département de faire du numérique un levier de modernisation de l’administration sanitaire. « Le ministère s'est engagé dans la transformation numérique à travers la mise en œuvre de solutions destinées à améliorer la gouvernance sanitaire, faciliter le travail des professionnels de santé et offrir de meilleurs services aux citoyens. La plateforme que nous lançons vient consolider cette dynamique. Elle s'inscrit dans notre vision d'un système de santé moderne, accessible, transparent, performant et centré sur les besoins des citoyens. Elle participe à la mise en œuvre de la Stratégie nationale de santé digitale » , a-t-il déclaré. À l’occasion de cette cérémonie, le ministère de la Santé a remis des agréments et des conventions de partenariat aux organisations JHPIEGO, au Centre d’initiative contre la drépanocytose et à Komalen’ho. Ces structures figurent parmi les premiers bénéficiaires de la plateforme, leurs demandes ayant été introduites, instruites et validées entièrement en ligne. Directeur pays de JHPIEGO, le Dr Jérémie Zoungrana s’est félicité de cette réforme, qu’il juge profondément transformatrice. « Entre la nouvelle procédure et l'ancienne, c'est le jour et la nuit. On a moins de papiers à remplir. On les remplit en ligne, on téléverse les documents en ligne et on effectue le suivi en ligne. Il n'y a pas de déplacement, le temps de traitement est rapide, le suivi est facilité et il n'y a pas d'intermédiaire. La différence se situe au niveau du gain de temps, de la qualité du traitement et aussi du fait qu'on n'est plus frustrés de ne pas savoir où se trouvent les documents. Il y a de la transparence dans la gouvernance, c'est une bonne gouvernance et on est plus satisfaits », a-t-il témoigné. Avec le lancement d' E-Agrement , le ministère de la Santé franchit une nouvelle étape dans sa transformation numérique. En misant sur la dématérialisation des procédures, il entend renforcer la transparence, réduire les délais de traitement des dossiers et rapprocher davantage l'administration sanitaire des usagers. ​ Saydou Ismaël GANAME Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : Le ministère de la Santé lance E-agrement, sa plateforme de gestion des procédures est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: As Pressure Mounts, U.S. Hunts for Cuba’s Next Leader
L’intelligence artificielle crée pour la première fois des virus qui fonctionnent et détruisent des bactéries résistantes
items.description: Des chercheurs de l'Universite Stanford et de l'Arc Institute ont reussi, pour la premiere fois, a creer a l'aide de l'intelligence artificielle de nouveaux virus capables d'attaquer des bacteries, selon un article publie par le Financial Times . Au total, 16 d'entre eux ont fonctionne lors des essais en laboratoire. Ces virus sont appeles bacteriophages. Ils s'attaquent aux bacteries et non aux cellules humaines. Les scientifiques les etudient depuis longtemps comme un moyen de lutter contre certaines infections, notamment lorsque les antibiotiques deviennent moins efficaces. Pour cette experience, les chercheurs ont utilise deux modeles d'intelligence artificielle, Evo 1 et Evo 2. Leur principe rappelle celui des outils capables de generer du texte, mais ici, l'IA travaille avec les informations contenues dans l'ADN. Elle analyse d'enormes quantites de donnees avant de proposer de nouvelles combinaisons. Le modele Evo avait ainsi etudie environ neuf mille milliards d'elements composant l'ADN, provenant d'animaux, de plantes, de micro-organismes et de virus. Les scientifiques sont ensuite partis d'un virus naturel connu, appele ΦX174, qui attaque la bacterie Escherichia coli. L'IA en a propose des milliers de nouvelles versions. Environ 300 ont ete testees en laboratoire et 16 ont reellement fonctionne. Une piste face a la resistance aux antibiotiques Les essais ont montre que plusieurs de ces nouveaux virus etaient plus efficaces que le virus naturel utilise au depart. Certains ont detruit les bacteries plus rapidement. Un melange de plusieurs d'entre eux a egalement reussi a attaquer trois variantes d'E. coli sur lesquelles ΦX174 ne fonctionnait plus. C'est la que cette technologie pourrait devenir particulierement utile. Certaines bacteries resistent de mieux en mieux aux traitements classiques, ce qui pousse les chercheurs a chercher d'autres moyens de les combattre. L'une de ces methodes est la phagotherapie. Elle consiste a utiliser des virus pour cibler et detruire certaines bacteries responsables d'infections. Cette approche est loin d'etre nouvelle. Avant la generalisation des antibiotiques, les bacteriophages etaient deja etudies pour combattre les infections. Apres la Seconde Guerre mondiale, la recherche et l'utilisation de ces virus ont notamment continue en URSS. Cette methode a egalement continue a etre utilisee dans plusieurs pays d'Europe de l'Est. L'intelligence artificielle pourrait aujourd'hui accelerer le developpement de cette methode ancienne. Au lieu de chercher dans la nature un virus capable d'attaquer une bacterie precise, les chercheurs pourraient utiliser l'IA pour creer plus rapidement un virus adapte a leur cible. Selon l'equipe de Stanford, cette possibilite pourrait devenir particulierement importante avec la progression des infections resistantes aux antibiotiques. Des questions de securite Les chercheurs ont toutefois pris plusieurs precautions. Pour preparer leur systeme, ils n'ont pas utilise de donnees sur l'ADN humain ni sur des virus capables d'infecter l'etre humain. Les tests ont egalement ete realises sur une variante d'E. coli qui ne provoque pas de maladie. Brian Hie, qui dirige le projet, a explique que ces precautions avaient ete prises volontairement. Malgre cela, cette technologie suscite deja des inquietudes. Des outils similaires pourraient un jour etre utilises pour creer des virus ou des microbes dangereux. Thomas Inglesby et Moritz Hanke, experts en securite sanitaire a l'Universite Johns-Hopkins, estiment notamment que les regles actuelles ne suivent pas encore le rythme de developpement de ces technologies. L'experience marque ainsi une nouvelle etape dans l'utilisation de l'intelligence artificielle en biologie. Pour la premiere fois, un systeme de ce type a permis de creer le code genetique complet d'un virus capable de fonctionner. Cette avancee pourrait etre utile en medecine, mais elle oblige aussi les chercheurs et les autorites a mieux encadrer son utilisation.
